B. Sales increased but profitability decreased.
C. The company raised its prices faster than its costs.
D. Energy costs fell by four per cent.

Corrigé

1. B — Sales increased but profitability decreased.. Le chiffre d'affaires (« turnover ») progresse, mais la marge (« operating margin shrank ») recule. L'option 3 inverse la cause : ce sont les coûts qui ont augmenté plus vite que les prix.

Exercice 3 — B2-M2-L5-I3 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez ce bulletin d'information économique en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie. (Entreprises fictives.)

Transcription :

Rosa DelgadoIn business news this morning: Talbridge Foods has agreed to acquire Merrin Dairies in a deal worth three hundred and forty million euros. The takeover would create the country's second-largest dairy group, with combined annual revenue of about one point two billion euros.
Rosa DelgadoMerrin's shareholders approved the offer yesterday, and Talbridge shares rose by three per cent on the news. However, the deal is still subject to approval by the national competition authority, which is expected to give its decision in the spring.
Rosa DelgadoThe announcement has raised concerns among staff. Unions fear that two of Merrin's five plants could close, as they produce similar products to Talbridge sites nearby.
Rosa DelgadoSpeaking to reporters, Talbridge's chief executive said there would be no compulsory redundancies for at least two years, and that any changes would be discussed with employee representatives. She did not, however, rule out closing sites in the longer term.

1. What is the main news?
A. Merrin Dairies has bought Talbridge Foods.
B. Two dairy companies have cancelled their merger.
C. Talbridge Foods has agreed to buy Merrin Dairies.
D. The competition authority has approved a merger.

2. What has Talbridge's chief executive promised?
A. No compulsory job cuts for at least two years
B. No site closures at any time in the future
C. Higher wages for Merrin's employees
D. A decision on the plants by the spring

Corrigé

1. C — Talbridge Foods has agreed to buy Merrin Dairies.. « Talbridge Foods has agreed to acquire Merrin Dairies ». L'option 1 inverse acheteur et cible ; l'option 4 est fausse car l'accord de l'autorité de la concurrence est encore attendu.
2. A — No compulsory job cuts for at least two years. « no compulsory redundancies for at least two years ». L'option 2 est le piège : elle « n'a pas exclu » des fermetures à plus long terme.

Exercice 4 — B2-M2-L5-I4 (C1, B2.1)

Faux amis. Choisissez le mot anglais qui traduit correctement l'idée entre parenthèses.

The [1] _____ cost of the project (le coût réel) was twenty per cent higher than the budget. One [2] _____ of the new system (un avantage) is that it reduces paperwork. We may [3] _____ (éventuellement) open an office in Spain, but nothing is decided. After long negotiations, the two firms [4] _____ (finalement) agreed on a price. Our [5] _____ (notre entreprise) employs three hundred people.

[1] current / actual / present / topical

[2] profit / benefice / benefit / gain of

[3] eventually / possibly / finally / lastly

[4] possibly / actually / eventually / lately

[5] society / company / firm of / corporation of

Corrigé

[1] actual. « actual » = réel, effectif. « current » signifie actuel : c'est justement le faux ami à éviter dans l'autre sens.
[2] benefit. « benefit » = avantage. « profit » serait un bénéfice financier, ce qui n'a pas de sens pour une réduction de paperasse.
[3] possibly. « éventuellement » = possibly (ou perhaps). « eventually » est un faux ami : il signifie « finalement ».
[4] eventually. « eventually » = finalement, après un long processus. « actually » signifie « en fait ».
[5] company. Une entreprise = « a company ». « society » désigne la société au sens collectif ou une association.

title: B2-M2 — Classe virtuelle : simulation de conférence téléphonique et débriefing d'écoute
description: Restituer oralement, après une conférence simulée à quatre participants, la problématique, la position de chaque intervenant et l'issue de l'échange. Identifier au moins deux énoncés implicites (refus poli, réserve, ironie) et en expliquer le sens réel. Comparer sa prise de notes avec celle d'un pair et corriger au moins une erreur d'attribution (qui a dit quoi).

sections.title: B2-M2-L6 — Classe virtuelle : simulation de conférence téléphonique et débriefing d'écoute
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Restituer oralement, après une conférence simulée à quatre participants, la problématique, la position de chaque intervenant et l'issue de l'échange.
  • Identifier au moins deux énoncés implicites (refus poli, réserve, ironie) et en expliquer le sens réel.
  • Comparer sa prise de notes avec celle d'un pair et corriger au moins une erreur d'attribution (qui a dit quoi).

Compétence C1 — niveau B2.2 — 40 min — classe virtuelle

Cette classe virtuelle met en pratique toutes les stratégies d'écoute du module dans une situation proche de la réalité : une conférence à plusieurs voix, avec des positions qui s'opposent, des sous-entendus et des chiffres. C'est un entraînement pédagogique : il ne donne lieu à aucun score de certification, mais à un retour précis sur votre manière d'écouter et de restituer.

Avant la séance

  • Réécoutez la vidéo de cette leçon et faites l'exercice d'écoute en deux parties ci-dessous.
  • Préparez votre grille de prise de notes : une ligne Problématique, une colonne par participant (position / argument / évolution), une ligne Implicite et une ligne Issue et actions.
  • Révisez les marqueurs des leçons 2 et 3 : I'm coming round to…, I'd be surprised if…, Let's park that, I'll see what I can do.

Pendant la séance

  1. Écoute en direct. Le formateur et trois apprenants volontaires jouent une conférence téléphonique à partir de fiches de rôle (caméras coupées, comme dans un vrai appel audio). Les autres apprenants prennent des notes avec leur grille.
  2. Restitution. Chaque apprenant résume en 60 secondes : la problématique, la position de chaque participant, l'issue. Le groupe vérifie les attributions : Was it Graham or Felix who suggested the second courier?
  3. Chasse à l'implicite. Le formateur rejoue trois répliques ambiguës ; vous expliquez leur sens réel et l'indice qui vous a guidé (lexique, intonation, pause).
  4. Deuxième simulation, avec d'autres rôles : cette fois, les auditeurs posent une question de clarification en direct (Sorry, could you clarify whether…?), comme dans une vraie réunion.

Ce qui est observé

  • l'exactitude des attributions (qui propose, qui s'oppose, qui décide) ;
  • la distinction entre une décision prise, une proposition et un report ;
  • l'interprétation correcte des sous-entendus ;
  • la précision des données relevées (chiffres, dates, quantités) ;
  • la clarté de la restitution orale.

Les erreurs les plus fréquentes, que le formateur relèvera : attribuer à un participant une idée qu'il a seulement rapportée (Graham said that the lab wanted…), prendre un report (Let's revisit it next month) pour une décision, confondre fifteen et fifty, ou retenir la première position d'un intervenant alors qu'il a changé d'avis en cours d'appel.

Après la séance, comparez votre grille avec la transcription fournie par le formateur, notez vos deux principales sources d'erreur et réalisez l'activité pratique du module.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Sorry, could you clarify whether…?Pardon, pourriez-vous préciser si… ?demander une clarification en direct
Just to check I've got this right: …Pour vérifier que j'ai bien compris : …reformuler
Was it Graham or Felix who suggested…?Est-ce Graham ou Felix qui a proposé… ?vérifier une attribution
As far as I understood, the decision was…Si j'ai bien compris, la décision était…restituer une issue
She seemed reluctant to…Elle semblait réticente à…décrire une attitude
In the end, they agreed to…Finalement, ils se sont mis d'accord pour…conclure une restitution

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
couriertransporteur, service de messagerieThe courier delivered the samples four hours late.
cold chainchaîne du froidAny break in the cold chain ruins the samples.
temperature logrelevé de températureThe temperature log showed a peak of twelve degrees.
incident reportrapport d'incidentYuki filed an incident report on Monday.
to switch (supplier)changer (de fournisseur)We could switch to another courier.
service level agreement (SLA)accord de niveau de serviceThe SLA guarantees delivery within six hours.
penalty clauseclause de pénalitéThe contract includes a penalty clause for late delivery.
to trialtester, mettre à l'essaiLet's trial the second courier on one route.
proctoringsurveillance d'examen à distanceOnline proctoring raises privacy concerns.
to roll backrevenir en arrière, annuler (un changement)We can roll back if the trial fails.
attributionattribution (de propos)Check the attribution: who actually said it?

Dialogue : Faut-il changer de transporteur ? Un appel à quatre voix

Conférence téléphonique chez Lumacore Biosciences après deux incidents de rupture de la chaîne du froid lors du transport d'échantillons. La directrice de projet anime ; logistique, qualité et finance s'expriment.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Isabel MorenoThanks for joining at short notice. We've had two cold-chain incidents in three weeks, so the question is whether we keep our current courier.Merci d'être venus au pied levé. Nous avons eu deux ruptures de la chaîne du froid en trois semaines ; la question est donc de savoir si nous gardons notre transporteur actuel.
Yuki TanakaFrom a quality point of view, two incidents is two too many. The temperature log showed twelve degrees for almost an hour on Tuesday.Du point de vue qualité, deux incidents, c'est deux de trop. Le relevé de température a affiché douze degrés pendant près d'une heure mardi.
Graham FowlerI don't disagree, Yuki, but they've been reliable for four years. Both incidents happened on the new airport route.Je ne dis pas le contraire, Yuki, mais ils sont fiables depuis quatre ans. Les deux incidents ont eu lieu sur le nouvel itinéraire de l'aéroport.
Felix AdlerAnd switching isn't cheap. The alternative courier quoted around thirty per cent more.Et changer ne coûte pas rien. L'autre transporteur a fait un devis environ trente pour cent plus cher.
Yuki TanakaWith respect, Felix, losing a batch of patient samples would cost a great deal more than that.Sauf votre respect, Felix, perdre un lot d'échantillons de patients coûterait bien plus que cela.
Isabel MorenoGraham, what did the current courier say about the airport route?Graham, qu'a dit le transporteur actuel au sujet de l'itinéraire de l'aéroport ?
Graham FowlerThey've promised to add a refrigerated van on that route. Whether they actually do it is another matter.Ils ont promis d'ajouter une camionnette réfrigérée sur cet itinéraire. Qu'ils le fassent vraiment, c'est une autre histoire.
Felix AdlerSo what if we trialled the second courier on the airport route only? That would limit the extra cost.Et si nous testions le second transporteur uniquement sur l'itinéraire de l'aéroport ? Cela limiterait le surcoût.
Yuki TanakaI could live with that, as long as the trial includes a penalty clause and daily temperature logs.Je pourrais m'en accommoder, à condition que l'essai comprenne une clause de pénalité et des relevés de température quotidiens.
Graham FowlerI'm coming round to it too. It also keeps the pressure on our current courier.Je m'y rallie aussi. Cela maintient en plus la pression sur notre transporteur actuel.
Isabel MorenoGood. So we're agreed: a two-month trial with the second courier on the airport route, starting on the first.Bien. Nous sommes donc d'accord : un essai de deux mois avec le second transporteur sur l'itinéraire de l'aéroport, à partir du premier.
Isabel MorenoFelix, could you check the budget? Yuki, please draft the quality requirements. Graham will brief both couriers.Felix, pourriez-vous vérifier le budget ? Yuki, merci de rédiger les exigences qualité. Graham informera les deux transporteurs.
Felix AdlerI'll see what I can find in the budget, but don't expect miracles.Je verrai ce que je peux trouver dans le budget, mais ne vous attendez pas à des miracles.
Isabel MorenoNoted. Let's speak again in two weeks. Thanks, everyone.C'est noté. Reparlons-en dans deux semaines. Merci à tous.

Déroulé de la classe virtuelle

  1. 5 min — Accueil, objectifs, rappel de la grille de prise de notes (problématique / positions / implicite / issue) et des règles de la simulation.
  2. 10 min — Simulation 1 : conférence audio à quatre voix (formateur + 3 volontaires, fiches de rôle) ; les autres apprenants prennent des notes. Restitution en 60 secondes par 2 ou 3 apprenants et vérification collective des attributions.
  3. 7 min — Chasse à l'implicite : le formateur rejoue 3 répliques ambiguës (refus poli, scepticisme, ironie) ; les apprenants en donnent le sens réel et l'indice.
  4. 10 min — Simulation 2 avec rotation des rôles ; les auditeurs posent une question de clarification en direct ; restitution en binômes.
  5. 8 min — Débriefing du formateur : erreurs d'attribution, décisions vs reports, chiffres ; conseils personnalisés ; consigne de l'activité pratique.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — B2-M2-L6-I1 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez cette conférence téléphonique entre quatre responsables d'un établissement d'enseignement, en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

Naomi ClarkeRight, we're all here. The question today is whether we move the end-of-year exams online with remote proctoring, or keep them on campus.
Peter LindqvistFrom an IT point of view, the platform is ready. We tested it with two hundred students in March without a single crash.
Sara HaddadThe technology isn't really my concern. Several students have told me they don't have a quiet room at home, and some are uncomfortable being filmed.
James OkoyeAnd realistically, booking the exam halls for three weeks costs us about forty thousand pounds. Online would save most of that.
Sara HaddadI'm not saying no. I'm saying we can't force it on everyone.
Naomi ClarkeSo what about giving students the choice? Online by default, but with campus rooms available for anyone who asks.
James OkoyeWe'd still save on the large halls. A few seminar rooms would be enough.
Sara HaddadThat I can support, provided that students can choose until two weeks before the exams.
Peter LindqvistFine by me. I'll prepare a short guide for students taking the exams online.

1. What is Sara's main concern in the first part?
A. The platform might crash during the exams.
B. Some students may not have suitable conditions at home.
C. The exam halls are too expensive to book.
D. Students have not been trained to use the platform.

2. What is finally decided?
A. All exams will stay on campus this year.
B. All exams will move online and the halls will be cancelled.
C. The decision is postponed until students have been consulted.
D. Exams will be online, with campus rooms on request.

Corrigé

1. B — Some students may not have suitable conditions at home.. « Several students… don't have a quiet room at home, and some are uncomfortable being filmed. » Elle écarte explicitement la question technique (« The technology isn't really my concern »), d'où le piège de l'option 1.
2. D — Exams will be online, with campus rooms on request.. Naomi propose « Online by default, but with campus rooms available for anyone who asks » ; James, Sara (avec une condition) et Peter acceptent. L'option 2 oublie l'option campus.

Exercice 2 — B2-M2-L6-I2 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez le message envoyé après l'appel sur le transporteur et répondez en quelques mots ou en chiffres.

Transcription :

Isabel MorenoHi all, a quick voice note to confirm what we agreed. The trial with the second courier will run for two months on the airport route only, starting on the first of next month. Yuki will send the quality requirements by Friday. Felix has found fifteen thousand euros in the logistics budget to cover the extra cost. And our next call is in two weeks, on the nineteenth.

1. Combien de temps durera l'essai ?

2. Sur quel itinéraire l'essai aura-t-il lieu ?

3. Quel montant Felix a-t-il trouvé dans le budget (en euros) ?

4. À quelle date aura lieu le prochain appel ?

Corrigé

1. two months / 2 months / deux mois / 2 mois. « The trial… will run for two months ».
2. the airport route / airport route / airport / aéroport / l'itinéraire de l'aéroport. « on the airport route only » : uniquement l'itinéraire de l'aéroport.
3. 15000 / 15,000 / 15 000 / fifteen thousand / 15000 euros / €15,000. « fifteen thousand euros » : 15 000 €, et non 50 000 (fifty).
4. the nineteenth / 19 / 19th / le 19 / the 19th. « on the nineteenth » : le 19.

Exercice 3 — B2-M2-L6-I3 (C1, B2.2)

Complétez ces notes de restitution d'une conférence téléphonique avec le mot correct.

The call was about whether to [1] _____ courier after two incidents. Yuki was clearly in favour of a change, while Graham was [2] _____ to drop a supplier that had been reliable for four years. Felix was worried about the cost, but he [3] _____ the idea of a trial on one route. In the end, Graham came round to the idea, and they [4] _____ on a two-month trial.

[1] switch / swap to / move of / turn

[2] eager / reluctant / delighted / keen

[3] put forward / turned down / put off / called off

[4] agreed / accepted / decided to / approved of

Corrigé

[1] switch. « to switch courier / supplier » = changer de transporteur / fournisseur. « move of » est agrammatical.
[2] reluctant. « reluctant to » = réticent à : Graham défendait le transporteur actuel. « keen » et « eager » diraient l'inverse.
[3] put forward. « to put forward an idea » = proposer une idée : c'est Felix qui suggère l'essai. « turned down » signifierait qu'il l'a refusée.
[4] agreed. « to agree on something » = se mettre d'accord sur. « accepted on » et « approved of on » sont agrammaticaux.

title: B2-M2 — Bilan du module : Compréhension d'échanges complexes
description: Ce module entraîne l'apprenant à comprendre les idées principales et les nuances d'échanges professionnels complexes : conférences téléphoniques à plusieurs voix, débats entre deux interlocuteurs, sous-entendus et changements de ton, monologues longs et chiffrés. Il consolide le vocabulaire de la vie économique de l'entreprise et se termine par une classe virtuelle de simulation de conférence.

sections.title: Quiz de validation du module (corrigé)
sections.contentHtml:
Seuil de réussite : 70 %.

Exercice 1 — B2-M2-Q1 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez la phrase et répondez à la question.

Transcription :

Brian KellyWe could look at your proposal again once the new financial year starts, but I wouldn't hold your breath.

1. What does the speaker suggest?
A. The proposal has been approved.
B. The proposal will be examined next week.
C. The new financial year starts very soon.
D. The proposal is unlikely to be accepted.

Corrigé

1. D — The proposal is unlikely to be accepted.. « I wouldn't hold your breath » = n'y comptez pas trop : la proposition a peu de chances d'aboutir. L'option 2 retient seulement « look at your proposal again ».

Exercice 2 — B2-M2-Q2 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez la phrase et répondez à la question.

Transcription :

Alicia RomeroDespite a fall in demand, the group managed to protect its margin by cutting overheads and renegotiating its supplier contracts.

1. How did the group protect its margin?
A. By reducing fixed and purchasing costs
B. By increasing its prices across all products
C. By increasing demand
D. By selling a subsidiary

Corrigé

1. A — By reducing fixed and purchasing costs. « by cutting overheads (frais généraux) and renegotiating its supplier contracts (coûts d'achat) ». La demande a baissé (« Despite a fall in demand »), ce qui exclut l'option 3.

Exercice 3 — B2-M2-Q3 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez l'animatrice d'une conférence téléphonique et répondez à la question.

Transcription :

Rebecca StoneLet's park the pricing question for now and come back to it once Daniela has joined. In the meantime, Tariq, could you take us through the launch plan?

1. What will happen next?
A. Daniela will join the call immediately.
B. The group will discuss pricing.
C. Tariq will present the launch plan.
D. The call will end.

Corrigé

1. C — Tariq will present the launch plan.. « Tariq, could you take us through the launch plan? » La question des prix est reportée (« Let's park ») jusqu'à l'arrivée de Daniela.

Exercice 4 — B2-M2-Q4 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez la phrase et répondez à la question.

Transcription :

Erik HalvorsenI was against the merger at first, but having seen the savings we could make on the purchasing side, I've changed my mind.

1. What is the speaker's position now?
A. He is still against the merger.
B. He now supports the merger.
C. He has not yet seen the figures.
D. He wants to postpone the decision.

Corrigé

1. B — He now supports the merger.. « I was against… at first, but… I've changed my mind » : il soutient désormais la fusion. L'option 1 correspond à sa position initiale.

Exercice 5 — B2-M2-Q5 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez ce dialogue entre deux acheteurs et répondez aux trois questions.

Transcription :

Karin HoltMarco, the question is whether we accept Delvar's new price list or put the contract out to tender.
Marco BelliniA seven per cent increase is a lot, but they haven't missed a single delivery in five years.
Karin HoltTrue, but seven per cent on a two-million-euro contract is a hundred and forty thousand euros.
Marco BelliniI know. Still, a tender takes four months, and there's no guarantee we'd find anyone as reliable.
Karin HoltWhat if we used the tender as leverage? We could tell Delvar we're consulting the market.
Marco BelliniThat might bring them down to four or five per cent. I'd be fine with that.
Karin HoltLet's draft the message together this afternoon.
Marco BelliniFine. But let's keep it polite. We still want them as a partner.

1. What is the issue?
A. Whether to accept a price rise or seek other offers
B. How to reduce delivery delays
C. Which department should manage the contract
D. Whether to sign a five-year contract with the supplier

2. What is Marco's attitude towards the supplier?
A. He thinks they are too expensive to keep.
B. He wants to end the relationship quickly.
C. He doubts their reliability.
D. He values them despite the price rise.

3. What do they decide to do?
A. Launch a full tender immediately
B. Accept the seven per cent increase without discussion
C. Use a possible tender to negotiate
D. Ask a new supplier for a quote

Corrigé

1. A — Whether to accept a price rise or seek other offers. « whether we accept Delvar's new price list or put the contract out to tender ». Les « five years » renvoient à l'historique de fiabilité, pas à la durée d'un contrat (option 4).
2. D — He values them despite the price rise.. « they haven't missed a single delivery in five years » et « We still want them as a partner ». C'est Karin qui insiste sur le coût (option 1).
3. C — Use a possible tender to negotiate. « use the tender as leverage… tell Delvar we're consulting the market » : la menace d'un appel d'offres sert de levier de négociation. Aucun appel d'offres n'est réellement lancé (option 1).

Exercice 6 — B2-M2-Q6 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez ce dialogue entre deux chercheurs et répondez aux trois questions. Attention aux sous-entendus.

Transcription :

Tim AshbyLeah, did you get a chance to read my abstract for the Vienna conference?
Leah MorganI did. The methodology section is very… thorough.
Tim AshbyIs that a polite way of saying it's too long?
Leah MorganLet's say the reviewers only spend a few minutes on each abstract, and your results don't appear until the last paragraph.
Tim AshbySo you'd move the results up?
Leah MorganI'd put the main finding in the second sentence, and I'd cut the methodology by half.
Tim AshbyHalf? That's a lot of work before Friday's deadline.
Leah MorganIt is. But I'd be surprised if it got accepted as it stands.

1. What does Leah mean when she calls the methodology section "very thorough"?
A. She thinks it is the best part.
B. She thinks it is too long.
C. She thinks it lacks detail.
D. She hasn't read it carefully.

2. What does Leah recommend?
A. Submitting to a different conference
B. Asking for a later deadline
C. Presenting the main result much earlier
D. Adding more methodology details

3. What does Leah imply at the end?
A. The abstract will certainly be accepted.
B. The deadline will be extended.
C. Tim should give up.
D. It will probably be rejected unchanged.

Corrigé

1. B — She thinks it is too long.. La pause avant « thorough » et la réaction de Tim (« a polite way of saying it's too long? »), qu'elle ne dément pas, montrent une critique implicite. L'option 1 prend le compliment au pied de la lettre.
2. C — Presenting the main result much earlier. « I'd put the main finding in the second sentence ». Elle recommande au contraire de réduire la méthodologie de moitié (option 4).
3. D — It will probably be rejected unchanged.. « I'd be surprised if it got accepted as it stands » = en l'état, il sera probablement refusé. Elle ne lui conseille pas d'abandonner (option 3), mais de le retravailler.

Exercice 7 — B2-M2-Q7 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez cette conférence téléphonique entre trois responsables d'une entreprise industrielle, en deux parties. Répondez à une question par partie.

Transcription :

Rebecca StoneOK, let's get going. The board wants a recommendation by Friday on the second assembly line. Dmitri, where do we stand?
Dmitri VolkovDemand is clearly there. We turned down three large orders last quarter because we simply didn't have the capacity.
Priyanka ShahI don't doubt the demand. The problem is timing. Interest rates have gone up, and borrowing eight million now would cost us far more than it would have a year ago.
Dmitri VolkovWe could lease the equipment instead of buying it. That would cut the upfront cost.
Priyanka ShahLeasing is more expensive over ten years, but it would protect our cash flow. I could accept that.
Rebecca StoneSo our recommendation is to go ahead with the second line, financed by leasing. Priyanka, could you prepare the figures for Friday?
Priyanka ShahWill do.

1. What is Priyanka's concern?
A. There is not enough demand for a second line.
B. The company has turned down too many orders.
C. The board needs more time to decide.
D. Borrowing has become more expensive.

2. What will the team recommend?
A. Building the line and leasing the equipment
B. Postponing the line until interest rates fall
C. Buying the equipment with a bank loan
D. Accepting fewer orders

Corrigé

1. D — Borrowing has become more expensive.. « Interest rates have gone up, and borrowing eight million now would cost us far more ». Elle dit explicitement « I don't doubt the demand », ce qui écarte l'option 1.
2. A — Building the line and leasing the equipment. « go ahead with the second line, financed by leasing ». Le prêt bancaire (option 3) est précisément ce que Priyanka voulait éviter.

Exercice 8 — B2-M2-Q8 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez cet échange entre une directrice de magasin et son responsable régional, en deux parties. Répondez à une question par partie.

Transcription :

Ian FraserWendy, I've seen the mystery shopper report. How do you feel about it?
Wendy ColeHonestly? Seventy-two per cent isn't where we want to be. But the visit was on the day the tills went down, so it's not entirely representative.
Ian FraserI understand. Still, the comments about staff not greeting customers have nothing to do with the tills.
Wendy ColeThat's fair. We've had four new starters this month, and I haven't had time to train them properly.
Ian FraserThen let's fix that. I can send our regional trainer for two days next week.
Wendy ColeThat would make a real difference. And could we schedule another visit in a month?
Ian FraserGood idea. Let's see what the next report says.

1. How does Wendy react to the report at first?
A. She is pleased with the score.
B. She rejects all the comments made in the report.
C. She admits it's poor but partly explains it.
D. She blames the area manager.

2. What does Ian offer?
A. To cancel the next visit
B. Training support for the new staff
C. Four new members of staff
D. New tills for the store

Corrigé

1. C — She admits it's poor but partly explains it.. « Seventy-two per cent isn't where we want to be » (elle reconnaît) + « the visit was on the day the tills went down » (circonstance atténuante). Elle ne rejette pas tout (option 2) : elle accepte ensuite la remarque d'Ian.
2. B — Training support for the new staff. « I can send our regional trainer for two days next week ». Les « four new starters » sont déjà arrivés ; Ian n'en propose pas d'autres (option 3).

Exercice 9 — B2-M2-Q9 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez ce briefing d'un directeur commercial, en deux parties. Répondez à une question par partie.

Transcription :

Gregory WellsGood morning, everyone. Over the past three years, sales of new instruments have levelled off, while our service contracts have grown by around fifteen per cent a year. Customers increasingly prefer to pay for results rather than to own equipment.
Gregory WellsSo, from January, all our laboratory analysers will also be available as a subscription, including maintenance, software updates and consumables.
Gregory WellsWhat does this mean for you? First, your bonuses will no longer be based on one-off sales, but on the annual value of the contracts you sign. Training on the new model will take place in February.
Gregory WellsYour immediate priority is to contact the fifty customers whose maintenance contracts end next year and present the subscription offer to them before the summer.

1. What trend has led to the new strategy?
A. Equipment sales are flat while services grow.
B. Customers have complained about maintenance costs.
C. Competitors have cut the price of their analysers.
D. Sales of consumables have fallen sharply.

2. What will change for the sales teams?
A. They will only sell to new customers.
B. They will stop visiting customers.
C. They will be trained by customers in February.
D. Their bonuses will be calculated differently.

Corrigé

1. A — Equipment sales are flat while services grow.. « sales of new instruments have levelled off, while our service contracts have grown by around fifteen per cent a year ». Les consommables (option 4) font partie de la nouvelle offre, aucune baisse n'est mentionnée.
2. D — Their bonuses will be calculated differently.. « your bonuses will no longer be based on one-off sales, but on the annual value of the contracts ». La formation de février s'adresse aux commerciaux, elle n'est pas donnée par les clients (option 3).

Exercice 10 — B2-M2-Q10 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez la présentation des résultats annuels d'une directrice des achats, en deux parties. Répondez à une question par partie.

Transcription :

Maria JohanssonThank you. Let me start with the results. This year, the purchasing department delivered savings of four point two million euros. That's a solid result, but it's below our target of five million.
Maria JohanssonThe main reason is energy. We had planned to save almost a million on our electricity contract, but market prices rose before we could renegotiate.
Maria JohanssonFor next year, the target remains five million. Where will it come from? Indirect spending: IT, travel, consultants and facilities. These categories represent about thirty per cent of our total spend, but only ten per cent of our savings so far.
Maria JohanssonSo I'll be asking each department head to nominate a contact person for indirect purchases by the end of the month.

1. What does the speaker say about this year's savings?
A. They exceeded the target.
B. They fell short of the target.
C. They came entirely from energy contracts.
D. They were twice last year's result.

2. Where will the department focus next year?
A. On renegotiating its electricity contract
B. On raw materials
C. On indirect costs like IT and travel
D. On reducing the number of buyers

Corrigé

1. B — They fell short of the target.. « four point two million… below our target of five million ». L'énergie est au contraire la raison du manque à gagner (option 3).
2. C — On indirect costs like IT and travel. « Indirect spending: IT, travel, consultants and facilities », qui pèse 30 % des dépenses mais seulement 10 % des économies. L'énergie (option 1) concernait l'année écoulée.

Exercice 11 — B2-M2-Q11 (C1, B2.1)

Complétez ce bulletin économique avec le terme correct.

Kestrin Group reported a 6% rise in [1] _____ last year, but its operating [2] _____ fell from 9% to 7% because of higher energy costs. The group also announced a [3] _____ freeze until June, although the chief executive ruled out any [4] _____.

[1] benefit / turnover / stake / headcount

[2] charges / share / margin / overheads

[3] hiring / hire / hired / employment of

[4] resignations / redundancies / dismissals of / turnovers

Corrigé

[1] turnover. Une hausse de 6 % du chiffre d'affaires = « turnover ». « benefit » est un faux ami (avantage).
[2] margin. « operating margin » s'exprime en pourcentage (9 % → 7 %). « overheads » désigne des frais, pas un ratio.
[3] hiring. Expression figée : « a hiring freeze » = un gel des embauches.
[4] redundancies. « to rule out redundancies » = exclure des licenciements économiques. Les « resignations » (démissions) ne dépendent pas de la direction.

Exercice 12 — B2-M2-Q12 (C1, B2.1)

Complétez ce compte rendu de conférence téléphonique avec le mot correct.

Several participants were [1] _____ mute at the start of the call. Anna explained that the main [2] _____ was whether to delay the launch. Tom was clearly against a delay, while Mia [3] _____ on the fence. In the end, the decision was [4] _____ until the next call.

[1] in / at / on / under

[2] problematic / issue / subject of / matter about

[3] sat / stood / stayed / kept

[4] delayed / cancelled / postponed / retarded

Corrigé

[1] on. « to be on mute » = avoir le micro coupé. « in mute » est un calque.
[2] issue. « the main issue was whether… » = la question principale était de savoir si… « problematic » est un adjectif en anglais.
[3] sat. Expression figée : « to sit on the fence » = ne pas prendre position (prétérit : sat).
[4] postponed. « the decision was postponed » = la décision a été reportée. « cancelled » signifierait qu'il n'y aura pas de décision.

sections.title: Mise en situation : Fiche d'écoute d'un échange professionnel authentique
sections.contentHtml:
Compétence C1 — 20 min

Choisissez un enregistrement authentique en anglais de 3 à 5 minutes lié à votre secteur (ingénierie, commerce, achats, sciences ou enseignement) : extrait de webinaire, présentation de résultats d'une entreprise, table ronde, débat ou épisode de podcast économique. Le formateur peut vous en proposer un si vous le souhaitez. Écoutez-le deux fois au maximum, sans transcription, puis complétez la fiche d'écoute du module : (1) la problématique formulée sous forme de question ; (2) les intervenants et la position de chacun, avec son argument principal ; (3) deux énoncés implicites ou nuancés et leur sens réel ; (4) trois données chiffrées, en précisant s'il s'agit de résultats ou de prévisions ; (5) l'issue ou le message principal ; (6) dix termes de la vie économique entendus, avec leur traduction.

Livrable : La fiche d'écoute complétée (en français pour l'analyse, en anglais pour les citations et les termes), accompagnée du lien ou de la référence de l'enregistrement et des minutages (début et fin de l'extrait).

Critères d'évaluation :

  • La problématique est formulée comme une question à trancher, et non comme un simple thème.
  • La position et l'argument principal de chaque intervenant sont correctement attribués.
  • Deux énoncés implicites ou nuancés sont cités en anglais et interprétés de façon pertinente.
  • Trois données chiffrées sont relevées avec exactitude et qualifiées (résultat réel, tendance ou prévision).
  • L'issue ou le message principal est distingué des détails illustratifs.
  • Les dix termes économiques sont correctement orthographiés et traduits.

title: B2-M3 — Rapports d'activité et tableaux commentés
description: Identifier en moins de 3 minutes la tendance principale d'un rapport d'activité et la cause que lui attribue l'auteur. Distinguer dans un tableau commenté le chiffre global de l'explication qui le nuance (effet de moyenne, élément exceptionnel, facteur local). Repérer la recommandation et la décision demandée à la fin d'un rapport, avec l'échéance associée.
imageQuery: business English Rapports d'activité et tableaux commentés

sections.title: B2-M3-L1 — Rapports d'activité et tableaux commentés
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Identifier en moins de 3 minutes la tendance principale d'un rapport d'activité et la cause que lui attribue l'auteur.
  • Distinguer dans un tableau commenté le chiffre global de l'explication qui le nuance (effet de moyenne, élément exceptionnel, facteur local).
  • Repérer la recommandation et la décision demandée à la fin d'un rapport, avec l'échéance associée.

Compétence C2 — niveau B2.1 — 50 min

Un rapport d'activité ne se contente pas d'aligner des chiffres : il les commente. Au niveau B2, l'enjeu n'est plus de retrouver un nombre, mais de comprendre ce que l'auteur en conclut et quelles réserves il exprime.

1. Décrire une évolution. Les verbes de tendance sont précis : rise / increase / grow (hausse), fall / decline / drop (baisse), peak at (atteindre un pic), level off / stabilise (se stabiliser), fluctuate (fluctuer). Les adverbes indiquent l'ampleur : slightly, marginally (légèrement) ≠ sharply, significantly (fortement). Repérez aussi la référence de comparaison : up 9% on Q2 (par rapport au trimestre précédent) ≠ 14% year-on-year (par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente).

2. Expliquer une évolution. Les causes sont introduites par due to, owing to, as a result of, driven by, mainly because of. Les conséquences par resulting in, leading to, which means that. Un facteur qui annule partiellement un autre est introduit par offset by (compensé par).

3. Nuancer un chiffre global. C'est le cœur des questions B2. Les formules suivantes signalent que le chiffre principal cache une autre réalité :

  • this headline figure conceals / masks… (ce chiffre global masque…) ;
  • excluding / if we exclude… (hors…) ;
  • this result benefited from a one-off… (élément exceptionnel, non reconductible) ;
  • partly explained by (en partie seulement).

Quand vous lisez however, although, whereas, by contrast, ralentissez : la phrase qui suit contient souvent la bonne réponse.

4. Lire un tableau commenté. Comparez toujours trois colonnes : la période précédente, la période actuelle et l'objectif (target). Un indicateur peut s'améliorer tout en restant sous l'objectif. Dans un tableau, rate désigne un taux, median une médiane (et non une moyenne), backlog un retard accumulé.

5. Repérer la recommandation. La dernière partie (Outlook, Recommendations, Next steps) contient la décision demandée : I recommend…, A decision is requested…, I would welcome your views…. Vérifiez qui doit agir et avant quand.

Pièges fréquents : confondre la hausse trimestrielle et la hausse annuelle ; prendre une cause partielle pour la cause unique ; attribuer à l'auteur une action qu'il demande à d'autres.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Revenue was up 9% on the previous quarter.Le chiffre d'affaires est en hausse de 9 % par rapport au trimestre précédent.comparer avec la période précédente
This headline figure conceals a less favourable trend.Ce chiffre global masque une tendance moins favorable.annoncer une nuance importante
The increase was largely driven by new contracts.La hausse s'explique en grande partie par de nouveaux contrats.attribuer une cause principale
These gains were partly offset by higher freight costs.Ces gains ont été en partie compensés par la hausse des coûts de transport.signaler un effet contraire
Excluding the southern region, the average would have been close to target.Hors région sud, la moyenne aurait été proche de l'objectif.isoler un facteur local
A decision on both points is requested by 14 October.Une décision sur ces deux points est demandée d'ici le 14 octobre.formuler la demande finale d'un rapport

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
year-on-yearsur un an, en glissement annuelInterventions grew by 14% year-on-year.
gross marginmarge bruteThe gross margin fell from 31% to 27%.
forecastprévisionRevenue was slightly above the forecast.
targetobjectif chiffréCustomer satisfaction remained below target.
first-time fix ratetaux de résolution à la première interventionThe first-time fix rate dropped to 79%.
turnaround timedélai de traitementMedian turnaround rose to 52 hours.
backlogretard accumulé, travail en attenteThe backlog should be cleared within two weeks.
one-offexceptionnel, non récurrentThe result includes a one-off grant.
to level offse stabiliserVolumes are expected to level off in spring.
to offsetcompenser, neutraliserSavings were offset by higher energy costs.
to account forreprésenter (une part de)Exports accounted for 42% of turnover.
buffer stockstock de sécuritéWe propose a buffer stock of critical parts.
outlookperspectivesThe outlook for Q4 remains positive.

Dialogue : Préparer la lecture d'un rapport trimestriel

Salle de réunion d'une société d'ingénierie, la veille d'un comité de direction. Le directeur des opérations relit le rapport trimestriel avec une contrôleuse de gestion.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Paul VennerInes, have you had a chance to look at Helena's Q3 report? I need to be clear about it before tomorrow's committee.Ines, as-tu eu le temps de regarder le rapport T3 d'Helena ? Je dois l'avoir bien en tête avant le comité de demain.
Ines KowalczykYes. At first glance it looks good: revenue is slightly above forecast and activity is up fourteen per cent year-on-year.Oui. À première vue, c'est bon : le chiffre d'affaires dépasse légèrement la prévision et l'activité progresse de quatorze pour cent sur un an.
Paul VennerAt first glance. I sense a 'but' coming.À première vue. Je sens qu'un « mais » arrive.
Ines KowalczykThere is one. The gross margin has dropped four points, mainly because of subcontracting over the summer.Il y en a un. La marge brute a perdu quatre points, surtout à cause de la sous-traitance cet été.
Paul VennerAnd the response times? The table shows almost eight hours against a target of six.Et les délais d'intervention ? Le tableau affiche presque huit heures pour un objectif de six.
Ines KowalczykThat's where you have to read the comment, not just the table. The problem is concentrated in the south. Excluding that region, we're close to target.C'est là qu'il faut lire le commentaire, pas seulement le tableau. Le problème est concentré dans le sud. Hors cette région, on est proche de l'objectif.
Paul VennerSo it's a local staffing issue rather than a general performance problem.Donc c'est un problème d'effectifs local plutôt qu'un problème de performance général.
Ines KowalczykExactly. Two senior technicians left in July and haven't been replaced.Exactement. Deux techniciens confirmés sont partis en juillet et n'ont pas été remplacés.
Paul VennerWhat about the first-time fix rate? It's going the wrong way too.Et le taux de résolution à la première intervention ? Il se dégrade aussi.
Ines KowalczykHelena says it's partly explained by parts shortages on the old HX-200 range. Note the word 'partly': it isn't the only cause.Helena dit que cela s'explique en partie par des pénuries de pièces sur l'ancienne gamme HX-200. Note le mot « en partie » : ce n'est pas la seule cause.
Paul VennerGood point. And what exactly is she asking us to decide?Bonne remarque. Et que nous demande-t-elle de décider exactement ?
Ines KowalczykTwo things: three recruitments in the south by the end of October, and a buffer stock of spare parts worth about a hundred and twenty thousand euros.Deux choses : trois recrutements dans le sud d'ici fin octobre, et un stock de sécurité de pièces détachées d'environ cent vingt mille euros.
Paul VennerThe stock ties up cash, but if it cuts repeat visits, it probably pays for itself.Le stock immobilise de la trésorerie, mais s'il réduit les interventions répétées, il est sans doute rentable.
Ines KowalczykThat's my reading too. I'll prepare a one-page summary of the figures for you tonight.C'est aussi ma lecture. Je te prépare ce soir une synthèse d'une page sur les chiffres.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — B2-M3-L1-I1 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez le rapport trimestriel puis répondez aux questions. Les questions suivent l'ordre du texte.

Corvane Engineering – Field Services Division
Q3 Activity Report (July–September)
Prepared by: Helena Marsh, Head of Field Services
Distribution: Executive Committee

  1. Overview

The division completed 1,184 maintenance interventions in Q3, up 9% on Q2 and 14% year-on-year. Revenue reached €4.6 million, slightly above the €4.5 million forecast. However, this headline figure conceals a less favourable trend: the gross margin fell from 31% to 27%, mainly because of higher subcontracting costs during the summer holiday period, when our own technicians were unavailable.

  1. Key indicators (Q2 / Q3 / Target)
  • First-time fix rate: 82% / 79% / 85%
  • Average response time (hours): 6.2 / 7.9 / 6.0
  • Customer satisfaction (out of 10): 8.4 / 8.1 / 8.5

The deterioration in response time is concentrated in the southern region, where two senior technicians left the company in July and have not yet been replaced. Excluding that region, the average response time would have been 6.4 hours, close to target. The drop in the first-time fix rate is partly explained by repeated shortages of spare parts for the older HX-200 pump range, which is no longer manufactured.

  1. Outlook and recommendations

Demand is expected to remain strong in Q4, as several industrial clients have brought forward their annual inspections. To protect margins, I recommend (a) approving the recruitment of three technicians for the southern region by the end of October, rather than continuing to rely on subcontractors, and (b) building a buffer stock of the twenty most frequently used HX-200 parts. The second measure would tie up approximately €120,000 in inventory, but it should significantly reduce the number of repeat visits. A decision on both points is requested at the committee meeting of 14 October.

1. What does the report say about Q3 revenue?
A. It was below forecast because of subcontracting costs.
B. It exceeded the forecast, but profitability declined.
C. It grew by 14% compared with the previous quarter.
D. It met the forecast and the margin improved.

2. According to the report, why did the average response time increase?
A. Technicians were on holiday in every region.
B. Spare parts for an old pump range were unavailable.
C. Clients brought forward their annual inspections.
D. Departures in one region had not been compensated.

3. What does the sentence beginning 'Excluding that region…' suggest?
A. The problem is largely local rather than company-wide.
B. The southern region performed better than the others.
C. The target of 6 hours is unrealistic for the whole division.
D. Response times improved everywhere except in the north.

4. What drawback of the second recommendation does the author mention?
A. It would delay the clients' annual inspections.
B. It would increase subcontracting costs.
C. It would tie up funds in inventory.
D. It would require the approval of the clients.

Corrigé

1. B — It exceeded the forecast, but profitability declined.. Le chiffre d'affaires (4,6 M€) dépasse légèrement la prévision, mais « this headline figure conceals a less favourable trend » : la marge brute baisse. L'option 3 est un piège : +14 % est la hausse sur un an (year-on-year) et concerne les interventions, pas le chiffre d'affaires par rapport au trimestre précédent.
2. D — Departures in one region had not been compensated.. « concentrated in the southern region, where two senior technicians left… and have not yet been replaced ». La pénurie de pièces (option 2) explique en partie la baisse du taux de résolution, pas le délai d'intervention.
3. A — The problem is largely local rather than company-wide.. Hors région sud, le délai moyen serait de 6,4 h, « close to target » : la dégradation est donc essentiellement locale. L'option 3 est tentante, mais le texte montre au contraire que l'objectif est presque atteint ailleurs.
4. C — It would tie up funds in inventory.. « would tie up approximately €120,000 in inventory » = immobiliserait des fonds en stock. La hausse de la sous-traitance (option 2) est le problème que la première recommandation cherche à résoudre.

Exercice 2 — B2-M3-L1-I2 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez ce commentaire de tableau de bord d'un laboratoire et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

To: Laboratory Leadership Team
From: Dr Owen Prior, Quality & Operations Lead, Lumera Biosciences
Subject: September dashboard – commentary

Please find below my commentary on the September dashboard, which I will present at Thursday's review.

Sample volumes: We processed 6,420 samples, a record month, driven by the start of the Delmar clinical study. Volumes are likely to stabilise at around 6,000 per month until the study ends in March.

Turnaround time: Median turnaround rose to 52 hours against a commitment of 48 hours. Although this looks worrying, the median masks two very different situations. Routine tests were in fact processed faster than in August (38 hours), whereas specialised assays took an average of 96 hours because one of our two mass spectrometers was out of service for eleven days. The instrument has now been repaired, and the backlog should be cleared within two weeks.

Error rate: The proportion of samples rejected for labelling errors fell to 0.6%, down from 1.1%, which suggests that the new barcode procedure introduced in July is working. I would not, however, draw firm conclusions from a single month.

Staffing: Overtime hours doubled compared with August. This is not sustainable beyond the end of the year. If volumes stay at the current level, we will need either one additional technician or a second shift on the spectrometers, which I estimate would cost roughly the same.

I would welcome your views on the staffing options before Thursday so that I can include costed scenarios in my presentation.

Owen

1. What was the main reason for the rise in sample volumes?
A. The launch of a clinical study
B. The repair of a mass spectrometer
C. A backlog carried over from August
D. The new barcode procedure

2. What point does Dr Prior make about the median turnaround time?
A. It shows that all tests were slower than in August.
B. It was within the 48-hour commitment.
C. It hides contrasting results by test type.
D. It will remain above 48 hours until March.

3. How does he interpret the fall in the error rate?
A. As proof that the barcode procedure has failed
B. As encouraging but not yet conclusive
C. As a direct result of the extra overtime
D. As a reason to change the July procedure

4. What does he ask the leadership team to do?
A. Approve overtime until March
B. Recruit a technician immediately
C. Prepare costed scenarios for Thursday
D. Give views on staffing options first

Corrigé

1. A — The launch of a clinical study. « a record month, driven by the start of the Delmar clinical study » : « driven by » introduit la cause. La réparation de l'appareil concerne le délai de traitement, pas les volumes.
2. C — It hides contrasting results by test type.. « the median masks two very different situations » : les tests de routine sont plus rapides, les analyses spécialisées beaucoup plus lentes. L'option 1 est le contresens le plus fréquent : les tests de routine ont au contraire accéléré.
3. B — As encouraging but not yet conclusive. « suggests that the new barcode procedure… is working. I would not, however, draw firm conclusions from a single month » : résultat encourageant, mais prudence. L'option 1 inverse le sens du texte.
4. D — Give views on staffing options first. « I would welcome your views on the staffing options before Thursday ». C'est lui-même qui préparera les scénarios chiffrés (« so that I can include costed scenarios ») : l'option 3 attribue l'action à la mauvaise personne.

Exercice 3 — B2-M3-L1-I3 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez cet extrait de rapport annuel d'un établissement d'enseignement et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Ashgrove College – Annual Report 2025–26
Section 4: Continuing Professional Education

Enrolments in our continuing professional education programmes reached 2,310 this year, compared with 2,050 in 2024–25, an increase of almost 13%. Growth was uneven across the portfolio. Short technical courses in industrial maintenance and electrical safety, mostly funded by employers, accounted for two thirds of the increase. By contrast, enrolments in the evening management diploma declined for the second consecutive year, falling from 180 to 146.

Completion rates remained high overall (91%), but the figure for fully online modules was noticeably lower, at 78%. Exit interviews indicate that learners who dropped out did not criticise the content; rather, they found it difficult to keep up without fixed session times. For this reason, from January the department will pilot a blended format, combining self-paced online work with a fortnightly live session.

Financially, the department generated a surplus of £212,000, which will be reinvested in equipment for the maintenance workshop. It should be noted that this result benefited from a one-off regional grant of £60,000 that will not be renewed next year.

Employer feedback was positive, with 87% of partner companies stating that they intend to send staff again. Several employers, however, asked for more flexible start dates, a request the department intends to address by offering monthly rather than termly intakes for the most popular courses.

Looking ahead, the department's priority is not to grow enrolments further but to consolidate quality, in particular by recruiting two experienced trainers in electrical engineering and by reviewing assessment methods across all technical courses.

1. What does the report say about the growth in enrolments?
A. It was evenly spread across all programmes.
B. It came mainly from employer-funded technical courses.
C. It was driven by the evening management diploma.
D. It was lower than in the previous year.

2. According to exit interviews, why did some online learners drop out?
A. They were dissatisfied with the course content.
B. Their employers stopped funding the modules.
C. They lacked a regular schedule to keep them on track.
D. The live sessions were too infrequent.

3. Why should the financial result be read with caution?
A. It includes a grant that will not recur.
B. It will be reinvested in equipment.
C. It is lower than in 2024–25.
D. It depends on employer feedback.

4. What is the department's main priority for next year?
A. Increasing enrolments in the management diploma
B. Expanding the number of fully online modules
C. Returning to termly intakes for all courses
D. Strengthening quality rather than volume

Corrigé

1. B — It came mainly from employer-funded technical courses.. « Short technical courses…, mostly funded by employers, accounted for two thirds of the increase ». Le diplôme de management du soir est justement en baisse (« By contrast… declined »).
2. C — They lacked a regular schedule to keep them on track.. « they found it difficult to keep up without fixed session times ». Le texte précise qu'ils ne critiquaient pas le contenu (« did not criticise the content ; rather… »), ce qui écarte l'option 1.
3. A — It includes a grant that will not recur.. « this result benefited from a one-off regional grant… that will not be renewed » : une partie de l'excédent est exceptionnelle. Le réinvestissement (option 2) est une utilisation de l'excédent, pas une réserve sur sa fiabilité.
4. D — Strengthening quality rather than volume. « the department's priority is not to grow enrolments further but to consolidate quality ». Les entrées mensuelles remplacent les entrées trimestrielles, et non l'inverse (option 3).

Exercice 4 — B2-M3-L1-I4 (C2, B2.1)

Complétez ce commentaire de résultats avec le terme exact choisi dans chaque liste.

Sales in the northern region [1] _____ at €2.1 million in May before falling slightly in June. Overall, export revenue [2] _____ for 42% of total turnover, compared with 35% last year. The increase was largely [3] _____ by new contracts in Scandinavia. However, higher freight costs partly [4] _____ these gains. Year-[5] _____-year, operating costs rose by only 1%, a [6] _____ increase given current inflation.

[1] peaked / summited / culminated / topped

[2] represented / accounted / made / counted

[3] pushed / carried / driven / led

[4] compensated / offset / overcame / balanced

[5] by / to / over / on

[6] marginally / margin / marginal / marginalised

Corrigé

[1] peaked. « to peak at + valeur » = atteindre un pic. « topped » exigerait « topped out at » ; « culminated » se construit avec « in » et ne s'emploie pas pour un chiffre.
[2] accounted. « to account for x% of » = représenter x % de. « represented » est correct sans « for » : « represented 42% ».
[3] driven. « driven by » = tiré par, porté par. « led » exigerait « led by » au sens de « dirigé par », ce qui ne convient pas pour une cause.
[4] offset. « to offset gains » = neutraliser des gains. « compensated » demande « for » (« compensated for ») et n'a pas ce sens négatif ici.
[5] on. Expression figée : « year-on-year » (en glissement annuel). On dit aussi « up 9% on Q2 ».
[6] marginal. Devant le nom « increase », il faut un adjectif : « a marginal increase » (une hausse minime). « marginally » est un adverbe.

title: B2-M3 — Analyses de marché : faits, prévisions et recommandations
description: Distinguer dans une analyse de marché de 300 mots ce qui relève d'un fait établi, d'une prévision et d'une recommandation. Identifier les moteurs de croissance et les freins (drivers / barriers) cités par l'auteur. Repérer le degré de certitude d'une affirmation à partir des marqueurs de prudence (is likely to, could, remains uncertain).
imageQuery: business English Analyses de marché : faits, prévisions et recommandations

sections.title: B2-M3-L2 — Analyses de marché : faits, prévisions et recommandations
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Distinguer dans une analyse de marché de 300 mots ce qui relève d'un fait établi, d'une prévision et d'une recommandation.
  • Identifier les moteurs de croissance et les freins (drivers / barriers) cités par l'auteur.
  • Repérer le degré de certitude d'une affirmation à partir des marqueurs de prudence (is likely to, could, remains uncertain).

Compétence C2 — niveau B2.1 — 50 min

Une analyse de marché mélange trois types d'énoncés qu'il faut absolument distinguer pour répondre juste.

1. Les faits établis sont au présent ou au passé, avec des données chiffrées et une source : The market was worth €340 million in 2025, Sales grew by 8% last year. Ils répondent aux questions « what is / what was ».

2. Les prévisions emploient le futur, des modaux ou des verbes d'attente : is expected to, is forecast to, is likely to, could, may. Leur degré de certitude varie :

  • forte probabilité : will almost certainly, is set to, is bound to ;
  • probabilité moyenne : is likely to, should, is expected to ;
  • simple possibilité : could, may, might ;
  • incertitude affichée : it remains unclear whether…, it is too early to say….

Une question B2 vous demandera souvent si l'auteur affirme une chose ou s'il la présente seulement comme possible. Une option qui transforme could en certitude est fausse.

3. Les recommandations apparaissent avec we recommend, we advise, the company should, it would be advisable to, priority should be given to. Elles sont souvent assorties de conditions : provided that, as long as, unless.

Structure habituelle : taille du marché (market size) et croissance (growth rate, CAGR), segments (segments), moteurs (drivers), freins (barriers, constraints), concurrence (competitive landscape, market share, new entrants), opportunités et menaces, puis recommandations.

Lire la concurrence. Les termes market leader, challenger, niche player situent les acteurs. Fragmented market = marché éclaté entre de nombreux acteurs ; consolidated market = dominé par quelques-uns. Barriers to entry = obstacles pour un nouvel entrant (coûts, normes, réseau de distribution).

Repérer l'opinion de l'analyste. Même un document « objectif » prend position : we believe, in our view, this is, in our opinion, overstated / underestimated. Les adjectifs évaluatifs (promising, modest, risky, attractive) donnent l'avis de l'auteur.

Méthode : lisez d'abord les intertitres et la conclusion, puis classez mentalement chaque phrase utile en F (fait), P (prévision) ou R (recommandation). Face à une question, demandez-vous de quelle catégorie relève la réponse attendue.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
The market is expected to grow by around 6% a year until 2030.Le marché devrait croître d'environ 6 % par an jusqu'en 2030.présenter une prévision
Growth is mainly driven by stricter energy regulations.La croissance est surtout portée par des réglementations énergétiques plus strictes.identifier un moteur de croissance
High upfront costs remain the main barrier to adoption.Le coût initial élevé reste le principal frein à l'adoption.identifier un frein
It remains unclear whether demand will hold up.On ne sait pas encore si la demande se maintiendra.exprimer une incertitude
In our view, the risk is often overstated.À notre avis, ce risque est souvent surestimé.donner la position de l'analyste
We recommend entering the market through a partnership, provided that…Nous recommandons d'entrer sur le marché via un partenariat, à condition que…formuler une recommandation conditionnelle

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
market sharepart de marchéThe leader holds about 30% market share.
compound annual growth rate (CAGR)taux de croissance annuel moyen (TCAM)The segment shows a CAGR of 7%.

to outpacecroître plus vite que, dépasserOnline sales outpaced store sales.
shelf spacelinéaire (en magasin)Retailers are reluctant to give shelf space to new brands.

Dialogue : Débriefer une étude de marché avec la direction

Visioconférence entre la directrice commerciale d'un fabricant de pompes et le consultant qui a rédigé l'étude de marché.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Marta LindholmKofi, thanks for the report. Before the board reads it, I want to be sure I separate the facts from your forecasts.Kofi, merci pour le rapport. Avant que le conseil le lise, je veux être sûre de séparer les faits de vos prévisions.
Kofi AsanteVery sensible. The facts are in section one: the industrial heat pump market for food processing was worth around three hundred and forty million euros last year.Très sage. Les faits sont dans la partie un : le marché des pompes à chaleur industrielles pour l'agroalimentaire pesait environ trois cent quarante millions d'euros l'an dernier.
Marta LindholmAnd the growth figure of nine per cent a year?Et le chiffre de neuf pour cent de croissance annuelle ?
Kofi AsanteThat's a forecast. We say growth is likely to reach nine per cent, mainly driven by stricter energy rules. It isn't guaranteed.C'est une prévision. Nous disons que la croissance atteindra probablement neuf pour cent, portée surtout par des règles énergétiques plus strictes. Ce n'est pas garanti.
Marta LindholmWhat could slow it down?Qu'est-ce qui pourrait la freiner ?
Kofi AsanteThe upfront cost is still the main barrier. Smaller plants find a payback period of five years hard to accept.Le coût initial reste le principal frein. Les petites usines ont du mal à accepter un retour sur investissement de cinq ans.
Marta LindholmYour report also mentions Asian competitors entering the market. Should we be worried?Votre rapport mentionne aussi l'arrivée de concurrents asiatiques. Devons-nous nous inquiéter ?
Kofi AsanteIn our view, that risk is somewhat overstated. They compete on price, but they don't yet have a local service network.À notre avis, ce risque est un peu surestimé. Ils jouent sur les prix, mais ils n'ont pas encore de réseau de service local.
Marta LindholmWhich is exactly our strength. And your recommendation?Ce qui est justement notre force. Et votre recommandation ?
Kofi AsanteWe recommend targeting medium-sized dairies first, provided that you can offer a financing package to reduce the upfront cost.Nous recommandons de cibler d'abord les laiteries de taille moyenne, à condition de proposer une offre de financement pour réduire le coût initial.
Marta LindholmSo the recommendation is conditional. Without financing, the strategy doesn't really work.Donc la recommandation est conditionnelle. Sans financement, la stratégie ne fonctionne pas vraiment.
Kofi AsanteThat's a fair reading. I'd make that point very clearly to the board.C'est une lecture juste. Je présenterais ce point très clairement au conseil.
Marta LindholmI will. Fact, forecast, recommendation. That's how I'll structure my summary.Je le ferai. Fait, prévision, recommandation. C'est ainsi que je structurerai ma synthèse.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — B2-M3-L2-I1 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez cet extrait d'analyse de marché puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Tessaline Consulting – Market Brief for Halvorsen Pumps
Industrial heat pumps in the food-processing sector

Market size and growth
The European market for industrial heat pumps used in food processing was worth an estimated €340 million in 2025, a 7% increase on the previous year. Dairies and breweries represent more than half of installed capacity, as both need large volumes of hot water at moderate temperatures, which is where heat pumps are most efficient. We expect the market to grow by around 9% a year until 2030, although this forecast depends heavily on energy prices and on the pace at which national subsidy schemes are rolled out.

Drivers and barriers
The main driver is regulation: from 2028, food plants above a certain size will have to report their heat-related emissions, and many have already started to replace gas boilers. The main barrier, by contrast, is financial. A typical installation costs between €400,000 and €900,000, and payback periods of four to six years remain hard to justify for smaller plants, whose investment horizon rarely exceeds three years.

Competitive landscape
The market remains fragmented. The three largest suppliers hold about 45% of the market between them, while dozens of regional installers share the rest. Several Asian manufacturers have entered the market with prices up to 20% lower. In our view, the threat they pose is somewhat overstated in the short term: buyers in this sector place a high value on fast on-site service, and none of these new entrants yet has a maintenance network in Europe.

Recommendation
We recommend that Halvorsen Pumps focus first on medium-sized dairies, where its service network gives it a clear advantage, provided that a leasing or energy-performance contract can be offered to reduce the upfront cost.

1. Why do dairies and breweries account for a large share of the market?
A. They receive higher subsidies than other plants.
B. Their heat needs suit heat pumps particularly well.
C. They were the first sector required to report emissions.
D. They usually have longer investment horizons.

2. How does the author present the 9% annual growth figure?
A. As a confirmed result for 2025
B. As a target set by national governments
C. As a projection that depends on external factors
D. As the growth already achieved by the market leaders

3. What is the analyst's view of the Asian manufacturers?
A. They lack local service, so they pose no immediate threat.
B. They will soon dominate the market thanks to lower prices.
C. They already hold about 45% of the market.
D. They should be approached as potential partners.

4. What condition is attached to the recommendation?
A. Halvorsen must build a maintenance network first.
B. Subsidy schemes must be in place before 2028.
C. Halvorsen must lower its prices by 20%.
D. A financing formula must reduce the initial investment.

Corrigé

1. B — Their heat needs suit heat pumps particularly well.. « both need large volumes of hot water at moderate temperatures, which is where heat pumps are most efficient ». L'obligation de déclaration (option 3) concerne toutes les usines au-delà d'une certaine taille, à partir de 2028.
2. C — As a projection that depends on external factors. « We expect… although this forecast depends heavily on energy prices and… subsidy schemes » : c'est une prévision conditionnelle. Le chiffre confirmé pour 2025 est +7 % (option 1).
3. A — They lack local service, so they pose no immediate threat.. « the threat… is somewhat overstated in the short term… none of these new entrants yet has a maintenance network in Europe ». Les 45 % (option 3) sont la part des trois plus grands fournisseurs.
4. D — A financing formula must reduce the initial investment.. « provided that a leasing or energy-performance contract can be offered to reduce the upfront cost ». Le réseau de maintenance existe déjà : c'est l'avantage de Halvorsen (option 1).

Exercice 2 — B2-M3-L2-I2 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez cette note d'analyse rédigée par une responsable de catégorie dans la grande distribution et répondez aux questions.

Brightmoor Retail – Category Insight Note
Refillable household cleaning products
Author: Leah Okonjo, Category Manager, Home Care

Situation
Refill stations for household cleaning products were installed in twelve of our stores in March as a six-month trial. Over that period, refill sales reached £186,000, which represents just 3% of the category in those stores. On the face of it, this is a modest result. However, the figure needs to be put in context: two thirds of refill customers were new to the category in our stores, and their average basket was 18% higher than that of other home care shoppers.

Market trends
Nationally, the refill segment is small but growing quickly, with sales up by roughly a third last year according to industry panels. Consumer surveys consistently show strong interest in reducing packaging. It would be unwise, though, to read too much into survey results: many shoppers say they are willing to change their habits but, in practice, choose the most convenient option. Our own data confirm this gap, since refill sales fell by almost half in stores where the station was placed at the back of the aisle.

Constraints
Refill stations take up about four metres of shelf space and require daily cleaning, which store managers see as a significant burden. Two suppliers have also warned that they cannot guarantee stock continuity if the network grows faster than planned.

Proposal
Rather than a national roll-out, I propose extending the trial to thirty stores with a high proportion of urban, younger customers, placing the stations near the store entrance, and reviewing the results in six months. A national decision could then be taken on firmer evidence.

1. Why does Leah Okonjo think the £186,000 result should not be judged too quickly?
A. Because it is higher than in other retailers' stores
B. Because the trial lasted only three months
C. Because refill shoppers were new and spent more
D. Because it represents a third of the category

2. What is her attitude towards consumer surveys?
A. She considers them the most reliable source available.
B. She is cautious, as intentions differ from behaviour.
C. She thinks they underestimate interest in refills.
D. She believes they are irrelevant to cleaning products.

3. Which piece of evidence from Brightmoor's own data supports her point?
A. Sales fell where stations were less visible.
B. Store managers asked for more refill stations.
C. Suppliers increased their stock levels.
D. Younger customers bought fewer refills.

4. What does she recommend?
A. An immediate national roll-out with new suppliers
B. Stopping the trial because of the cleaning burden
C. Moving all stations to the back of the aisle
D. A bigger, better-targeted trial first

Corrigé

1. C — Because refill shoppers were new and spent more. « two thirds of refill customers were new to the category… their average basket was 18% higher ». « A third » (option 4) correspond à la croissance nationale du segment, pas à la part de la catégorie (3 %).
2. B — She is cautious, as intentions differ from behaviour.. « It would be unwise… to read too much into survey results: many shoppers say they are willing… but, in practice, choose the most convenient option ». Elle les relativise sans les rejeter totalement (option 4).
3. A — Sales fell where stations were less visible.. « refill sales fell by almost half in stores where the station was placed at the back of the aisle » : la commodité l'emporte sur l'intention. Les responsables de magasin voient au contraire la station comme une contrainte (option 2).
4. D — A bigger, better-targeted trial first. « Rather than a national roll-out, I propose extending the trial to thirty stores… A national decision could then be taken on firmer evidence ». « Rather than » écarte explicitement l'option 1.

Exercice 3 — B2-M3-L2-I3 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez cette analyse de marché interne d'un fabricant d'instruments scientifiques et répondez aux questions.

Pelham Instruments – Strategy Team
Benchtop bioreactors for teaching laboratories: market assessment

Purpose
This note assesses whether Pelham should launch a simplified benchtop bioreactor aimed at universities and technical colleges, a segment we do not currently serve.

Demand
Teaching laboratories increasingly want students to work on equipment similar to what they will use in industry. Our interviews with 24 heads of department show clear interest: 19 said they would consider buying such a unit within three years. Interest, however, is not the same as budget. Most institutions buy large equipment only when they obtain a specific capital grant, and grant cycles are slow and unpredictable. We therefore estimate realistic annual demand at 150 to 200 units in Europe, well below the figure suggested by the interviews alone.

Competition
Two established suppliers already sell research-grade systems to universities, but at prices (above €40,000) that teaching departments can rarely afford. A small start-up offers a low-cost unit at around €9,000; it is popular with lecturers but has a reputation for unreliable software. A product priced between €15,000 and €18,000, with robust software and a teaching package, would therefore occupy a gap in the market.

Risks
The main risk is cannibalisation: some research customers might choose the cheaper teaching model instead of our standard system. We consider this risk limited, as the teaching unit would lack the data-logging precision that research users need. A second risk is that development could take longer than the planned eighteen months if we redesign the software from scratch.

Conclusion
The opportunity is real but modest. We recommend a go decision only if development costs can be kept below €1.2 million by reusing the existing control software.

1. Why does the strategy team estimate demand below what the interviews suggest?
A. Several heads of department refused to be interviewed.
B. Institutions rely on irregular grants for equipment.
C. Students prefer to train on industrial equipment.
D. The start-up has already captured most of the market.

2. What gap in the market does the note identify?
A. A mid-priced, reliable teaching product
B. A research-grade system for under €9,000
C. A low-cost unit with no software
D. A data-logging upgrade for existing systems

3. How does the team assess the risk of cannibalisation?
A. As the main reason not to launch the product
B. As impossible to estimate at this stage
C. As limited, since researchers need more precision
D. As serious, because research customers want lower prices

4. What is the overall recommendation?
A. Launch the product immediately
B. Abandon the project because demand is too low to justify it
C. Redesign the software before deciding
D. Proceed only if reusing software keeps costs down

Corrigé

1. B — Institutions rely on irregular grants for equipment.. « Interest, however, is not the same as budget… grant cycles are slow and unpredictable ». L'intérêt existe (19 sur 24), mais le financement limite les achats réels.
2. A — A mid-priced, reliable teaching product. Entre les systèmes de recherche (plus de 40 000 €) et l'unité de la start-up (9 000 €, logiciel peu fiable), un produit à 15 000–18 000 € avec un logiciel robuste occuperait un créneau. Les autres options inventent des produits non mentionnés.
3. C — As limited, since researchers need more precision. « We consider this risk limited, as the teaching unit would lack the data-logging precision that research users need ». Il est cité comme « main risk », mais jugé limité : l'option 1 confond importance et probabilité.
4. D — Proceed only if reusing software keeps costs down. « We recommend a go decision only if development costs can be kept below €1.2 million by reusing the existing control software ». Refaire le logiciel (option 3) est justement présenté comme un risque de retard.

Exercice 4 — B2-M3-L2-I4 (C2, B2.1)

Complétez ce résumé d'étude de marché avec le terme qui convient.

The market for laboratory consumables is highly [1] _____: no supplier holds more than 10% market [2] _____. Online sales have [3] _____ traditional distribution for three years in a row. Strict quality certification remains the main barrier to [4] _____ for new suppliers. Demand is [5] _____ to grow by 5% a year, although public procurement budgets could [6] _____ this trend.

[1] fragmented / broken / divided up / scattered

[2] part / portion / share / quota

[3] outpaced / outdated / overtaken by / outnumbered by

[4] entrance / entry / access to / enter

[5] waited / expected / hoped / foreseen

[6] to slow down / slow down / slowing down / slowed down

Corrigé

[1] fragmented. « a fragmented market » = un marché éclaté entre de nombreux acteurs, ce que confirme la suite (aucun fournisseur au-delà de 10 %). « broken » signifierait « cassé ».
[2] share. « market share » = part de marché. « part » est un faux ami dans cette expression.
[3] outpaced. « to outpace » = croître plus vite que. « overtaken by » inverserait le sens de la phrase.
[4] entry. Expression figée : « barrier to entry » (barrière à l'entrée).
[5] expected. « is expected to grow » = devrait croître (prévision). « is foreseen to » n'est pas idiomatique.
[6] slow down. Après le modal « could », on emploie la base verbale sans « to » : « could slow down this trend ». « to slow down » est l'erreur la plus fréquente (calque de « pourraient de… »).

title: B2-M3 — Cahiers des charges et appels d'offres
description: Distinguer dans un cahier des charges les exigences obligatoires (shall / must) des exigences souhaitables (should / may) sans erreur sur 5 exigences. Identifier dans un appel d'offres les critères d'attribution, leur pondération, l'échéance de remise et les motifs d'exclusion. Repérer dans un avis de clarification ce qui modifie ou ne modifie pas le dossier initial.
imageQuery: business English Cahiers des charges et appels d'offres

sections.title: B2-M3-L3 — Cahiers des charges et appels d'offres
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :
