sections.title: B2-M6-L5 — Mise en situation transversale : le dossier Fernhill Cycles
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Écouter une réunion de crise et identifier le problème, sa gravité et la position de chaque interlocuteur.
  • Lire l'email d'un distributeur et en dégager les demandes, l'ultimatum et sa condition.
  • Présenter oralement en 90 secondes une recommandation argumentée à la direction en s'appuyant sur les informations entendues et lues.
  • Rédiger un email de réponse au distributeur de 150 mots minimum qui reconnaît le problème, présente le plan d'action et répond à chaque demande.

Compétence C3 — niveau B2.2 — 45 min

Cette mise en situation transversale combine les quatre compétences autour d'une même étude de cas, comme dans une vraie journée de travail : vous écoutez une réunion, vous lisez un email, vous présentez une recommandation, puis vous rédigez une réponse. Il s'agit d'un entraînement interne de l'organisme, pas d'une épreuve du test VTest — dont les quatre compétences sont évaluées séparément ; l'intérêt ici est de mobiliser vos acquis dans une situation réaliste.

Le cas. Fernhill Cycles (entreprise fictive) fabrique des vélos à assistance électrique. Un défaut de connecteur de batterie touche son modèle Urbana 2 : le moteur peut se couper. Le plus gros distributeur de la marque, Velocity Bikes, menace de suspendre ses commandes. La direction doit choisir entre un rappel complet et un programme d'inspection ciblé.

Étape 1 — Écouter (C1). La responsable qualité et le directeur commercial discutent de la situation. Repérez : la fréquence du défaut, pourquoi il est grave, les deux options et leur coût, la préférence de chacun et la condition posée.

Étape 2 — Lire (C2). L'email du distributeur contient des faits, une demande de remboursement, un ultimatum conditionnel (unless…) et une demande de coordination. Notez chacun de ces éléments : vous en aurez besoin pour les étapes 3 et 4.

Étape 3 — Présenter (C3). En 90 secondes, recommandez une option à la direction. Une présentation B2 efficace :

  • annonce la recommandation dès la première phrase ;
  • s'appuie sur des faits précis issus de l'écoute et de la lecture (chiffres, coûts, délais) ;
  • reconnaît la faiblesse de l'option choisie (Admittedly…) ;
  • précise les conditions et les prochaines étapes.

Étape 4 — Rédiger (C4). Vous répondez au distributeur. Ici, le ton compte autant que le contenu : reconnaître le problème sans se défausser, présenter le plan, répondre à chaque demande (remboursement, coordination de la communication), proposer un échange. Vous réutiliserez les structures du module 5 : refus ou acceptation diplomatique, connecteurs de cause et de conséquence.

Conseil de méthode. Prenez des notes structurées pendant les étapes 1 et 2 : problème / chiffres / options / positions / demandes. Ce sont ces notes, et non votre mémoire, qui rendront votre présentation et votre email précis. C'est aussi une compétence professionnelle à part entière : transformer ce qu'on a entendu et lu en décision argumentée.

Temps conseillé : écoute 6 min, lecture 6 min, préparation et présentation 5 min, rédaction 25 min.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Just over three percent of the bikes have come back with the same fault.Un peu plus de trois pour cent des vélos sont revenus avec le même défaut.présenter un fait chiffré
It isn't a fire risk, but we can't ignore it.Ce n'est pas un risque d'incendie, mais nous ne pouvons pas l'ignorer.évaluer la gravité d'un problème
Unless we receive a clear action plan by the end of next week, we will suspend new orders.Si nous ne recevons pas de plan d'action clair d'ici la fin de la semaine prochaine, nous suspendrons les nouvelles commandes.ultimatum conditionnel
My recommendation is to launch a targeted inspection programme rather than a full recall.Je recommande de lancer un programme d'inspection ciblé plutôt qu'un rappel complet.annoncer une recommandation
We will, of course, reimburse the repair costs you have incurred.Nous vous rembourserons, bien entendu, les frais de réparation que vous avez engagés.répondre à une demande de remboursement
We would like any communication to customers to be coordinated with your teams.Nous souhaitons que toute communication aux clients soit coordonnée avec vos équipes.proposer une coordination

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
recallrappel (de produits)A full recall would cost about €1.2 million.
fault / defectdéfautThe same fault appeared on 3% of the bikes.
connectorconnecteurThe battery connector can loosen over time.
to cut outse couper, s'arrêter brusquementThe motor can cut out without warning.
dealerrevendeur, concessionnaireFree inspections will be carried out by dealers.
to take off the shelvesretirer des rayonsThe dealer threatened to take the model off its shelves.
to make headlinesfaire les gros titresA full recall would make headlines.
at one's own expenseà ses propres fraisThey repaired the bikes at their own expense.
to suspendsuspendreThey will suspend new orders.
action planplan d'actionPlease send us a clear action plan.
to reimburserembourserWe will reimburse your repair costs.
end customerclient finalCommunication to end customers must be coordinated.
to incur (costs)engager, supporter (des frais)We will cover the costs you have incurred.

Dialogue : Briefing : le dossier Fernhill Cycles

Capsule de présentation du cas, tournée dans le studio de l'organisme. La formatrice présente la mission à l'apprenant avant les quatre étapes.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Helen MarshKarim, for this last practice, you're joining the crisis team at Fernhill Cycles, a fictional e-bike maker.Karim, pour ce dernier entraînement, tu rejoins la cellule de crise de Fernhill Cycles, un fabricant fictif de vélos électriques.
Karim BenaliWhat's the crisis?Quelle est la crise ?
Helen MarshA battery connector on one model can loosen, and the motor cuts out. Their biggest dealer is losing patience.Un connecteur de batterie sur un modèle peut se desserrer, et le moteur se coupe. Leur plus gros revendeur perd patience.
Karim BenaliAnd what do I have to do?Et qu'est-ce que je dois faire ?
Helen MarshFour things. Listen to a meeting, read the dealer's email, present a recommendation to management, then reply to the dealer.Quatre choses. Écouter une réunion, lire l'email du revendeur, présenter une recommandation à la direction, puis répondre au revendeur.
Karim BenaliSo all four skills in one case.Donc les quatre compétences dans un seul cas.
Helen MarshExactly, like a real working day. The key is to take structured notes: problem, figures, options, positions, requests.Exactement, comme une vraie journée de travail. La clé, c'est de prendre des notes structurées : problème, chiffres, options, positions, demandes.
Karim BenaliWhy is that so important?Pourquoi est-ce si important ?
Helen MarshBecause your presentation and your email must use precise facts. 'About three percent' is far more convincing than 'some bikes'.Parce que ta présentation et ton email doivent s'appuyer sur des faits précis. « Environ trois pour cent » est bien plus convaincant que « quelques vélos ».
Karim BenaliIs this how the official test works?C'est comme ça que fonctionne le test officiel ?
Helen MarshNo. The official test assesses each skill separately. This case study is our own internal exercise to help you transfer your skills to real situations.Non. Le test officiel évalue chaque compétence séparément. Cette étude de cas est notre propre exercice interne, pour t'aider à transférer tes compétences en situation réelle.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — B2-M6-L5-I1 (C1, B2.2)

Étape 1 — Écouter. Dialogue long en deux parties : écoutez la réunion et répondez à la question de chaque partie. Prenez des notes pour les étapes suivantes.

Transcription :

Ingrid PaulsenMarco, the latest figures are in. Just over three percent of the Urbana 2 bikes sold since March have come back with the same battery connector fault.
Marco SilvaThree percent? That's far above our usual one percent. Is it a safety issue?
Ingrid PaulsenIt isn't a fire risk, fortunately. The connector loosens and the motor cuts out. But if that happens on a busy road, a rider could be put in danger, so we can't ignore it.
Marco SilvaAnd our largest dealer, Velocity Bikes, is already threatening to take the model off its shelves.
Ingrid PaulsenWe have two options. A full recall of all twelve thousand bikes would cost about one point two million euros. Or we could run a targeted programme: free inspections at dealers and a new connector only where needed, for roughly three hundred and fifty thousand.
Marco SilvaA recall would reassure the dealers, but it would also make headlines. I'd go for the targeted programme, as long as we contact every owner directly instead of waiting for them to come in.
Ingrid PaulsenAgreed, provided that our legal team confirms it meets our obligations. I'll ask them today.
Marco SilvaAnd I'll call Velocity this afternoon. They need to hear it from us before they hear it from their customers.

1. Why is the fault considered serious?
A. It could cause the battery to overheat and catch fire
B. The motor can cut out suddenly in traffic
C. It affects every Urbana 2 bike sold
D. Dealers are unable to repair it

2. What does Marco recommend?
A. A full recall of all the bikes
B. Waiting for customers to report problems
C. Replacing every connector at the factory before any new sales
D. A targeted inspection, with every owner contacted directly

Corrigé

1. B — The motor can cut out suddenly in traffic. « The connector loosens and the motor cuts out… a rider could be put in danger ». Le risque d'incendie est explicitement écarté (« It isn't a fire risk ») ; seuls un peu plus de 3 % des vélos sont concernés.
2. D — A targeted inspection, with every owner contacted directly. « I'd go for the targeted programme, as long as we contact every owner directly instead of waiting for them to come in ». Il écarte le rappel complet à cause de l'impact médiatique.

Exercice 2 — B2-M6-L5-I2 (C2, B2.1)

Étape 2 — Lire. Lisez l'email du distributeur et répondez aux trois questions. Notez ses demandes : vous y répondrez à l'étape 4.

From: Tom Ashby, Purchasing Director, Velocity Bikes
To: Marco Silva, Sales Director, Fernhill Cycles
Subject: Urbana 2 – customer returns

Marco,

Over the past two months, our 14 shops have received 46 Urbana 2 bikes with motor cut-outs. Our mechanics have identified the battery connector as the cause in almost every case. We have repaired them at our own expense so far, but this cannot continue.

To be clear, we have no wish to stop selling the Urbana range, which remains one of our best sellers. However, unless we receive a clear action plan by the end of next week, including reimbursement of our repair costs (€5,980 to date), we will suspend new orders of the Urbana 2 until the issue is resolved.

I would also ask that any communication to end customers be coordinated with us, as our shop staff are the first people they contact.

Regards,
Tom Ashby

1. What has Velocity Bikes done so far?
A. Returned the faulty bikes to Fernhill
B. Stopped selling the Urbana range
C. Repaired the bikes and paid for the repairs itself
D. Told customers to contact Fernhill directly

2. What will happen if Fernhill does not send a satisfactory plan by the end of next week?
A. Velocity will suspend new orders of the Urbana 2
B. Velocity will stop selling all Fernhill bikes
C. Velocity will take legal action
D. Velocity will send all the bikes back

3. What else does Tom ask for?
A. A discount on future orders
B. That customer communication be coordinated with Velocity
C. Training for his mechanics
D. A new model to replace the Urbana 2 free of charge for customers

Corrigé

1. C — Repaired the bikes and paid for the repairs itself. « We have repaired them at our own expense so far ». Tom précise au contraire qu'il ne souhaite pas arrêter de vendre la gamme Urbana.
2. A — Velocity will suspend new orders of the Urbana 2. « unless we receive a clear action plan… we will suspend new orders of the Urbana 2 until the issue is resolved ». La suspension est temporaire et ne concerne que ce modèle.
3. B — That customer communication be coordinated with Velocity. « I would also ask that any communication to end customers be coordinated with us » (subjonctif après ask that). Aucune remise ni formation n'est demandée.

Exercice 3 — B2-M6-L5-I3 (C3, B2.2)

Étape 3 — Présenter. 60 secondes de préparation, puis 90 secondes de réponse. Appuyez-vous sur vos notes des étapes 1 et 2 (chiffres, coûts, demandes du distributeur).

Question : You are a member of Fernhill Cycles' crisis team. Using what you heard and read, present your recommendation to management: which option should Fernhill choose and why, and what should be done for dealers such as Velocity Bikes? (préparation 60 s, réponse 90 s)

Langue utile : My recommendation is to… rather than… · Just over three percent of… · … would cost around…, whereas… · Admittedly, … · provided that… · As for dealers, … · To sum up: …

Corrigé

Critères : Recommandation annoncée dès la première phrase. ; Au moins trois faits précis tirés de l'écoute et de la lecture (pourcentage, coûts, demandes du distributeur). ; Concession sur la faiblesse de l'option choisie et condition posée. ; Mesures concrètes pour les distributeurs (remboursement, coordination, délai). ; Temps de parole : au moins 72 secondes sur 90 ; discours fluide et structuré.
Réponse modèle : My recommendation is to launch the targeted inspection programme rather than a full recall. Just over three percent of the Urbana 2 bikes sold since March are affected, and although the fault is not a fire risk, the motor can cut out in traffic, so we must act quickly. A full recall of twelve thousand bikes would cost around one point two million euros and would certainly make headlines, whereas the targeted programme would cost roughly three hundred and fifty thousand. Admittedly, a recall would reassure dealers more. That's why the programme must be credible: we should contact every owner directly, provided that our legal team confirms this meets our obligations. As for dealers, Velocity Bikes has already repaired forty-six bikes at its own expense, so I'd recommend reimbursing the five thousand nine hundred and eighty euros immediately and sending them the action plan this week, well before their deadline. Finally, all communication to customers should be coordinated with dealers, since they are the first people customers contact. To sum up: targeted programme, direct contact with owners, and full support for our dealers.

Exercice 4 — B2-M6-L5-I4 (C4, B2.1)

Étape 4 — Rédiger. 25 minutes conseillées, 150 mots minimum. Répondez à chaque demande de Tom Ashby.

Sujet : You are Marco Silva, Sales Director at Fernhill Cycles. Reply to Tom Ashby's email (step 2). Acknowledge the problem and thank Velocity Bikes for its support; present the action plan decided by Fernhill (targeted inspection programme, free new connectors, direct contact with all owners); confirm the reimbursement of the repair costs; answer his request about customer communication; suggest a call or meeting with a precise date. Write at least 150 words. — Rappel : ton à la fois responsable et rassurant, une réponse à chaque demande, action attendue datée.

email — 150 mots minimum, 25 minutes

  • J'ouvre par une reconnaissance du problème et un remerciement.
  • Le plan d'action est présenté avec une date de démarrage.
  • Le remboursement est confirmé avec le montant et les modalités.
  • Je réponds explicitement à la demande sur la communication clients.
  • Je propose un échange avec une date et une heure précises.
  • Le compteur affiche au moins 150 mots.

Corrigé

Critères : Respect du sujet : reconnaissance du problème, plan d'action, remboursement, communication clients et proposition d'échange datée. ; Chaque demande du distributeur reçoit une réponse explicite. ; Ton professionnel : responsable, sans se défausser, et orienté solution. ; Cohésion : connecteurs de cause, de conséquence et d'addition variés. ; Contrôle grammatical : futur, passif, relatives. ; Au moins 150 mots.
Production modèle :
Subject: RE: Urbana 2 – customer returns and action plan

Dear Tom,

Thank you for your email and for the detailed information from your mechanics. I fully understand your frustration, and I would like to thank your teams for supporting our customers while we investigated the issue.

We have now decided on a clear action plan. From 1 December, every Urbana 2 owner will be contacted directly and invited to book a free inspection at their dealer. Where necessary, the battery connector will be replaced with a new, redesigned part, which will be supplied to your shops free of charge, together with a fixed fee for each inspection.

In addition, we will reimburse the €5,980 you have spent on repairs so far. Please send us the invoices, and payment will be made within ten days.

As you requested, no message will be sent to end customers until it has been agreed with you, since your staff are their first point of contact.

Would you be available for a call on Thursday at 10:00 to go through the details?

Best regards,
Marco Silva
Sales Director, Fernhill Cycles

sections.title: B2-M6-L6 — Bilan et autoévaluation
sections.contentHtml:
Objectifs :

  • Comparer ses résultats aux quatre simulations et à l'étude de cas, et identifier sa compétence la plus fragile.
  • Formuler trois objectifs de préparation mesurables (activité, fréquence, critère de réussite).
  • Comprendre une autoévaluation rédigée en anglais et en repérer les décisions (au moins 3 questions sur 4).

Compétence C2 — niveau B2.1 — 15 min

Vous avez terminé les quatre simulations et l'étude de cas. Cette dernière leçon vous aide à faire le point et à préparer la suite, jusqu'au passage de la certification.

Rappel important : les résultats affichés dans votre espace sont des scores pédagogiques internes et des niveaux CECRL estimés. Ce ne sont pas des scores VTest et ils ne préjugent pas du résultat officiel, qui est déterminé uniquement par la plateforme du certificateur lors de votre passage. Un résultat officiel n'apparaît dans votre dossier que lorsque le relevé est transmis et enregistré avec sa pièce justificative.

Étape 1 — Relire vos résultats. Pour C1 et C2, regardez le nombre de bonnes réponses, mais surtout le type de question manqué : opinion d'un locuteur, condition, décision finale, nuance dans un article. Pour C3 et C4, relisez les retours du formateur : temps de parole utilisé, nuance de l'argumentation, cohésion, nombre de mots.

Étape 2 — Une priorité par compétence. Exemples au niveau B2 : je ne repère pas les conditions introduites par provided that (C1) ; je confonds proposition et décision dans les comptes rendus (C2) ; mes réponses de 2 minutes s'arrêtent vers 1 min 20 (C3) ; mes textes sont argumentés mais sans concession (C4).

Étape 3 — Trois objectifs mesurables. Un bon objectif dit quoi, à quelle fréquence et comment savoir que c'est réussi. Par exemple : Deux fois par semaine, je rédige un texte argumenté en 30 minutes et je dépasse 220 mots avec au moins une concession. Évitez les objectifs vagues comme améliorer mon écrit.

Conseils de préparation avant le passage

  • Gestion du temps : entraînez-vous toujours avec un minuteur. Pour l'écoute, l'audio peut être rejoué tant que le chronomètre tourne, mais chaque réécoute consomme du temps.
  • Seuil de mots : 150 mots en B2.1, 200 mots à partir de B2.2 ; si vous visez B2, prenez l'habitude de dépasser 200 mots.
  • Questions ouvertes : préparez vos structures (opinion – arguments – concession – condition – conclusion) et utilisez tout le temps de parole.
  • Conditions matérielles : micro, casque, connexion, endroit calme ; vérifiez le lien d'accès et les consignes transmises par le certificateur.
  • Régularité : vingt minutes par jour valent mieux que trois heures la veille.

L'exercice de cette leçon présente l'autoévaluation d'un autre apprenant, rédigée en anglais. Lisez-la, puis rédigez la vôtre dans l'activité pratique du module.

Langue clé

AnglaisFrançaisUsage
Overall, my listening has improved, but I still miss conditions introduced by 'provided that'.Dans l'ensemble, ma compréhension orale a progressé, mais je manque encore les conditions introduites par « provided that ».bilan nuancé
My strongest skill is reading, especially minutes and reports.Ma compétence la plus solide est la lecture, en particulier des comptes rendus et des rapports.point fort
My two-minute answers tend to stop too early.Mes réponses de deux minutes ont tendance à s'arrêter trop tôt.identifier un point faible
Twice a week, I will write a timed essay of over 220 words.Deux fois par semaine, je rédigerai une rédaction chronométrée de plus de 220 mots.objectif mesurable
These are internal estimates, not an official result.Ce sont des estimations internes, pas un résultat officiel.rappel du statut des scores

Vocabulaire

TermeTraductionExemple
self-assessmentautoévaluationWrite a short self-assessment after the simulations.
strengthpoint fortReading reports is one of my strengths.
area for improvementaxe d'améliorationMy main area for improvement is fluency.
to tend toavoir tendance àI tend to stop speaking too early.
measurable goalobjectif mesurableSet one measurable goal for each skill.
timed practiceentraînement chronométréTimed practice helps you manage stress.
estimated levelniveau estiméThe platform shows an estimated level, not an official score.
to keep track ofsuivre, garder une trace deKeep track of your word count in each essay.

Dialogue : Conseils : du bilan au plan de préparation

Capsule de conclusion dans le studio de l'organisme. La formatrice et l'apprenant font le bilan des simulations du parcours B2.

PersonnageRépliqueTraduction
Helen MarshSo, Karim, you've done all four simulations and the case study. What stands out?Alors, Karim, tu as fait les quatre simulations et l'étude de cas. Qu'est-ce qui ressort ?
Karim BenaliReading went well, especially the minutes. Listening was harder: I missed two questions about conditions.La lecture s'est bien passée, surtout les comptes rendus. L'écoute a été plus difficile : j'ai raté deux questions sur des conditions.
Helen MarshThat's useful to know. And speaking?C'est utile à savoir. Et l'oral ?
Karim BenaliThe project review was OK, but I stopped at about a minute and a half.La revue de projet allait bien, mais je me suis arrêté vers une minute trente.
Helen MarshSo what's your goal for speaking? Make it measurable.Alors, quel est ton objectif pour l'oral ? Rends-le mesurable.
Karim BenaliThree times a week, I answer a two-minute question with a timer and speak for at least a hundred seconds.Trois fois par semaine, je réponds à une question de deux minutes avec un chrono et je parle au moins cent secondes.
Helen MarshPerfect. And for writing?Parfait. Et pour l'écrit ?
Karim BenaliTwo timed essays a week, always above two hundred and twenty words, with at least one concession.Deux rédactions chronométrées par semaine, toujours au-dessus de deux cent vingt mots, avec au moins une concession.
Helen MarshExcellent. And remember, the levels on the platform are our internal estimates. Your official result will only come from the certifier.Excellent. Et souviens-toi, les niveaux affichés sur la plateforme sont nos estimations internes. Ton résultat officiel viendra uniquement du certificateur.
Karim BenaliUnderstood. A little every day until the test.Compris. Un peu chaque jour jusqu'au passage.

Exercices corrigés

Exercice 1 — B2-M6-L6-I1 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez l'autoévaluation d'un apprenant et répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte. Elle vous servira de modèle pour rédiger la vôtre.

From: Lucas Ferreira
To: Training team
Subject: Self-assessment after the B2 simulations

Hello,

Here is my self-assessment after the final simulations. Overall, my listening has improved a lot since the beginning of the course. I now follow long dialogues without difficulty; however, I still miss details when a speaker adds a condition at the end, for example with 'provided that'. From now on, I will replay only the final part of each recording when I hesitate, instead of the whole audio.

Reading is clearly my strongest skill. I finished all four documents with three minutes to spare and made only one mistake, on an expert's opinion in the article.

Speaking remains my main area for improvement. In the two-minute project review, I stopped after about 80 seconds because I had not planned the last part. Three times a week, I am going to practise with a timer, using four key words: purpose, status, problem, expectations.

Finally, my essay reached 214 words, but my trainer noted that it had no real concession. In my next essays, I will always include one paragraph presenting the opposite view.

Best regards,
Lucas

1. What is Lucas's remaining difficulty in listening?
A. He cannot follow long dialogues
B. He misses conditions added at the end
C. He replays every recording too often
D. He does not understand the specialised vocabulary

2. How did Lucas do in the reading simulation?
A. He did not have time to finish
B. He made several mistakes on the minutes
C. He finished early with a single error
D. He found the email the most difficult

3. What does Lucas plan to do for speaking?
A. Practise with a timer three times a week
B. Take individual lessons
C. Answer only short questions
D. Write his answers in full before speaking

4. What was the problem with Lucas's essay?
A. It was below the minimum number of words
B. It was off topic
C. It had too many connectors
D. It did not present the opposite point of view

Corrigé

1. B — He misses conditions added at the end. « I still miss details when a speaker adds a condition at the end, for example with 'provided that' ». Il précise au contraire qu'il suit désormais les dialogues longs sans difficulté.
2. C — He finished early with a single error. « I finished all four documents with three minutes to spare and made only one mistake », sur l'opinion de l'expert dans l'article, pas sur le compte rendu.
3. A — Practise with a timer three times a week. « Three times a week, I am going to practise with a timer, using four key words ». Il s'agit de mots clés, pas de réponses rédigées intégralement.
4. D — It did not present the opposite point of view. « it had no real concession » : il n'a pas présenté le point de vue opposé. Avec 214 mots, il dépasse le minimum de 200.

title: B2-M6 — Bilan du module : Mises en situation et bilan final
description: Ce module final propose quatre simulations internes de niveau B2 reprenant les familles d'activités du référentiel RS6905 (compréhension orale, compréhension écrite, expression orale, expression écrite), une mise en situation transversale fondée sur une étude de cas (écouter, lire, présenter, rédiger) et un bilan d'autoévaluation. Ce sont des entraînements pédagogiques conçus par l'organisme, et non le test VTest : ils servent à se familiariser avec les formats, à gérer son temps et à cibler les derniers points à consolider avant le passage.

sections.title: Quiz de validation du module (corrigé)
sections.contentHtml:
Seuil de réussite : 70 %.

Exercice 1 — B2-M6-Q1 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez l'annonce et choisissez la bonne réponse.

Transcription :

Finance ManagerPlease note that the deadline for submitting budget proposals has been brought forward to the twelfth, as the board meeting itself has been moved to the following Monday.

1. What has changed?
A. The board meeting has been cancelled
B. Budget proposals must now be submitted earlier
C. The budget has been reduced
D. The deadline has been postponed by a week

Corrigé

1. B — Budget proposals must now be submitted earlier. « brought forward to the twelfth » = avancé au 12. Le piège est de comprendre « reporté » : bring forward signifie avancer, pas repousser.

Exercice 2 — B2-M6-Q2 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez la réponse et choisissez ce que veut dire la personne.

Transcription :

Operations DirectorI'd normally say yes straight away, but given the timing, I'd rather we waited until the audit is finished before we commit to anything.

1. What does the speaker mean?
A. She agrees immediately
B. She refuses the proposal completely
C. She thinks the audit is unnecessary at this stage
D. She wants to wait for the audit to finish

Corrigé

1. D — She wants to wait for the audit to finish. « I'd rather we waited until the audit is finished before we commit » : elle préfère attendre, sans refuser. « I'd normally say yes » est une concession, pas un accord immédiat.

Exercice 3 — B2-M6-Q3 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez l'avis exprimé et choisissez la bonne réponse.

Transcription :

Purchasing ManagerAdmittedly, the new supplier is more expensive, but their defect rate is a fraction of what we're used to, so overall I think we'd actually save money.

1. What is the speaker's opinion of the new supplier?
A. It would save money overall despite higher prices
B. It is too expensive to be considered
C. Its quality is about the same as the current supplier's
D. It should be asked to lower its prices

Corrigé

1. A — It would save money overall despite higher prices. Concession (« Admittedly, … more expensive ») puis argument principal : moins de défauts, donc des économies au total. Le prix plus élevé n'est pas un motif de refus.

Exercice 4 — B2-M6-Q4 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez la note et répondez à la question.

From 1 March, visitors to the Delft laboratory will need to be registered at least 48 hours in advance. Same-day access will only be granted to emergency maintenance contractors, provided that they are accompanied by a member of the facilities team throughout their visit.

1. Who can enter the laboratory without being registered two days in advance?
A. Any visitor accompanied by a member of staff
B. Visitors arriving before 1 March
C. Escorted emergency maintenance contractors
D. Members of the facilities team only

Corrigé

1. C — Escorted emergency maintenance contractors. L'exception concerne uniquement les intervenants de maintenance d'urgence, à condition d'être accompagnés par l'équipe des services généraux. Un visiteur ordinaire, même accompagné, doit être enregistré.

Exercice 5 — B2-M6-Q5 (C2, B2.2)

Lisez l'extrait de compte rendu et répondez à la question.

S. Patel proposed moving the client workshop online to reduce costs. A. Moreno argued that the client had specifically asked for a face-to-face session. After discussion, it was agreed to keep the workshop in person but to shorten it from two days to one, thereby cutting travel and venue costs by about 40%.

1. What was decided?
A. To hold the workshop online
B. To cancel the workshop
C. To keep the two-day format
D. To hold a shorter face-to-face workshop

Corrigé

1. D — To hold a shorter face-to-face workshop. « agreed to keep the workshop in person but to shorten it from two days to one ». Le passage en ligne était la proposition initiale de S. Patel, non retenue.

Exercice 6 — B2-M6-Q6 (C2, B2.2)

Lisez l'extrait d'article et répondez à la question.

Many retailers have rushed to install self-service checkouts. Consumer researcher Dana Whitfield accepts that they reduce queues at peak times, but she warns that removing staff entirely is a mistake: 'Shoppers who need help and cannot find it simply go elsewhere, and that loss never appears in the savings figures.'

1. What is Dana Whitfield's position?
A. Self-service checkouts help, but cutting all staff can lose customers
B. Self-service checkouts should be removed from stores as soon as possible
C. Self-service checkouts increase queues
D. Retailers should hire more cashiers at peak times

Corrigé

1. A — Self-service checkouts help, but cutting all staff can lose customers. Elle concède un avantage (moins d'attente aux heures de pointe) mais met en garde contre la suppression totale du personnel. Elle ne demande pas le retrait des caisses automatiques.

Exercice 7 — B2-M6-Q7 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez l'email et répondez à la question.

Dear Ms Novak, thank you for your quotation, which we have reviewed carefully. While your proposal is technically excellent, it is 18% above our budget. Unless you can revise the price by Friday, we will unfortunately have to award the contract to another bidder. Kind regards, Tomas Berg

1. What is Tomas Berg's message?
A. The contract has already been awarded to a cheaper competitor
B. The proposal is accepted at the current price
C. Another bidder may win unless the price is cut by Friday
D. The technical proposal must be improved

Corrigé

1. C — Another bidder may win unless the price is cut by Friday. « Unless you can revise the price by Friday » : condition négative. La décision n'est pas encore prise, et la qualité technique est jugée excellente.

Exercice 8 — B2-M6-Q8 (C4, B2.2)

Choisissez la forme correcte.

By the end of the review, we expect to have [1] _____ a decision on the launch date.

[1] reach / reached / reaching / reaches

Corrigé

[1] reached. Futur antérieur après expect : « expect to have + participe passé » (reached).

Exercice 9 — B2-M6-Q9 (C4, B2.1)

Choisissez le connecteur correct.

[1] _____ being cheaper, the second option was rejected because of its longer lead time.

[1] Although / Because / Despite / Whereas

Corrigé

[1] Despite. Suivi d'une forme en -ing (being cheaper) et sens concessif : « Despite ». « Although » demanderait un sujet et un verbe (Although it was cheaper).

Exercice 10 — B2-M6-Q10 (C3, B2.1)

Complétez l'expression utile pour conclure une prise de parole.

Let me [1] _____ up the main points before we move on to the next item.

[1] make / put / take / sum

Corrigé

[1] sum. « to sum up » = résumer, récapituler. « put up » ou « take up » ont d'autres sens (afficher, occuper).

Exercice 11 — B2-M6-Q11 (C4, B2.2)

Choisissez la préposition correcte.

Profits rose [1] _____ €2.4 million this year, up from €2.1 million.

[1] by / of / to / at

Corrigé

[1] to. « rise to » + niveau atteint (2,4 M€). « rose by » introduirait l'écart (by €0.3 million).

sections.title: Mise en situation : Mon plan de préparation final
sections.contentHtml:
Compétence C4 — 20 min

À partir de vos résultats aux quatre simulations et à l'étude de cas (entraînements internes) et des retours du formateur, rédigez en anglais un email d'autoévaluation adressé à l'équipe pédagogique, sur le modèle de celui de Lucas : ce qui s'est bien passé, ce qui reste à consolider dans chaque compétence, et trois objectifs de préparation mesurables jusqu'à votre passage de la certification.

Livrable : Un email en anglais d'au moins 180 mots déposé sur la plateforme, contenant un bilan par compétence (C1, C2, C3, C4), au moins un point fort et un axe d'amélioration, et trois objectifs mesurables.

Critères d'évaluation :

  • Les quatre compétences sont évoquées, avec au moins un point fort et un axe d'amélioration.
  • Trois objectifs précisent l'activité, la fréquence et le critère de réussite.
  • Le bilan est nuancé (however, although, while) et s'appuie sur des faits précis (temps de parole, nombre de mots, type de question manqué).
  • Les formes du futur (will, be going to) sont correctement employées pour les décisions.
  • Le texte ne présente pas les scores internes comme un résultat officiel.

title: Entraînement au format VTest — banque de positionnement corrigée (A2 à C1)
description: Les 4 familles d'épreuves (écoute, lecture, oral, écrit) du niveau A2 au niveau C1, avec corrigés commentés, pour situer sa progression avant le passage du test.

sections.title: C1 — Écouter et comprendre un ensemble d'énoncés, de dialogues et de monologues en anglais
sections.contentHtml:
Exercice 1 — PL-C1-01 (C1, A2.1)

Écoutez l'annonce, puis choisissez la bonne réponse.

Transcription :

ReceptionistGood morning, everyone. Room 2A is closed today for cleaning, so the team meeting is in Room 4B at ten o'clock.

1. Where is the team meeting today?
A. In Room 2A
B. In Room 4B
C. In the cafeteria
D. At reception

Corrigé

1. B — In Room 4B. L'annonce dit « the team meeting is in Room 4B ». La salle 2A est citée, mais elle est fermée pour nettoyage : c'est le piège.

Exercice 2 — PL-C1-02 (C1, A2.1)

Écoutez le message, puis choisissez la bonne réponse.

Transcription :

LisaHi Tom, it's Lisa from Accounts. Can you send me the hotel invoice before Friday, please? I need it for your travel expenses.

1. What does Lisa ask Tom to do?
A. Send her an invoice
B. Call her back on Friday
C. Book a hotel for Friday
D. Pay for his travel

Corrigé

1. A — Send her an invoice. Lisa demande « send me the hotel invoice » (envoyer la facture d'hôtel). Les mots « hotel » et « Friday » apparaissent, mais elle ne demande ni réservation ni rappel.

Exercice 3 — PL-C1-03 (C1, A2.2)

Écoutez le dialogue, puis répondez aux trois questions.

Transcription :

DanielHello, Brightway Foods, this is Daniel. How can I help?
EmmaHi Daniel, it's Emma from Northwind Logistics. Your order of forty boxes will arrive tomorrow, not today. Our truck had a problem.
DanielOh, OK. What time tomorrow?
EmmaAround nine in the morning. Is someone at the warehouse then?
DanielYes, the warehouse opens at eight. That's fine.

1. Why is Emma calling?
A. To place an order
B. To say a delivery is late
C. To ask for a payment
D. To cancel her company's order

2. How many boxes did Brightway Foods order?
A. Fourteen
B. Four
C. Forty
D. Twenty-four

3. When does the warehouse open?
A. At eight
B. At nine
C. At ten
D. At midday

Corrigé

1. B — To say a delivery is late. Emma annonce que la commande arrivera « tomorrow, not today » : la livraison est retardée. Elle ne l'annule pas, elle la décale.
2. C — Forty. « Forty boxes » = 40. Attention à la confusion fréquente entre « forty » (40) et « fourteen » (14), dont l'accent tombe sur la fin.
3. A — At eight. Daniel dit « the warehouse opens at eight ». Neuf heures est l'heure de livraison prévue, pas l'heure d'ouverture.

Exercice 4 — PL-C1-04 (C1, A2.2)

Écoutez le dialogue, puis répondez aux trois questions.

Transcription :

JuliaExcuse me, I'm new here. Where can I print documents?
BenThere's a printer next to the kitchen. You need your staff card to use it.
JuliaI don't have my card yet. HR says it'll be ready on Wednesday.
BenNo problem. Send the file to me and I'll print it for you today.

1. Where is the printer?
A. In the HR office upstairs
B. At reception
C. Near the lifts
D. Next to the kitchen

2. What does Julia need to use the printer?
A. A password
B. Permission from HR
C. A USB key
D. Her staff card

3. What will Ben do?
A. Call HR
B. Lend her his staff card today
C. Print the document for her
D. Show her the kitchen

Corrigé

1. D — Next to the kitchen. Ben dit « next to the kitchen ». Le service RH est mentionné seulement pour la carte, pas pour l'imprimante.
2. D — Her staff card. « You need your staff card to use it » : il faut le badge du personnel. Les RH préparent la carte mais ne donnent pas d'autorisation.
3. C — Print the document for her. « Send the file to me and I'll print it for you » : il imprimera le document à sa place. Il ne lui prête pas sa carte.

Exercice 5 — PL-C1-05 (C1, B1.1)

Écoutez le dialogue, puis répondez aux trois questions.

Transcription :

AdamPriya, the client from Halden Engineering just emailed. They can't come on Tuesday because their flight was cancelled.
PriyaThat's a shame. We'd prepared the factory tour. Did they suggest another date?
AdamThey proposed Thursday afternoon, but you're at the trade fair then, aren't you?
PriyaYes, until Thursday evening. Could you ask if Friday morning works? I'd really like to be there.
AdamSure. I'll also check whether the meeting room is free.

1. Why can't the client come on Tuesday?
A. Their flight was cancelled
B. The factory is closed
C. Priya is on holiday
D. The meeting room is booked

2. Why is Thursday a problem?
A. Priya will be at a trade fair
B. The client has another meeting
C. The tour isn't ready
D. It's a public holiday

3. What will Adam do next?
A. Book a new flight for the client
B. Cancel the factory tour
C. Ask the client about Friday
D. Go to the trade fair

Corrigé

1. A — Their flight was cancelled. « Their flight was cancelled » : leur vol a été annulé. La salle de réunion n'est évoquée qu'à la fin, pour vendredi.
2. A — Priya will be at a trade fair. Priya est au salon professionnel (« trade fair ») jusqu'à jeudi soir. C'est le client qui a proposé jeudi : il n'est donc pas indisponible.
3. C — Ask the client about Friday. Priya lui demande « Could you ask if Friday morning works? » et il répond « Sure » : il va proposer vendredi au client. La visite n'est pas annulée, elle est déplacée.

Exercice 6 — PL-C1-06 (C1, B1.1)

Écoutez l'annonce, puis choisissez la bonne réponse.

Transcription :

Finance OfficerJust a reminder that from next Monday, all expense claims must be submitted through the new online portal. Paper forms will no longer be accepted, and claims older than sixty days won't be reimbursed.

1. What is changing next Monday?
A. Expense claims will be paid faster
B. The reimbursement limit will increase
C. Claims must be approved by a manager
D. Expense claims must be made online

Corrigé

1. D — Expense claims must be made online. « Must be submitted through the new online portal… paper forms will no longer be accepted » : les notes de frais passent en ligne. Le délai de 60 jours n'est pas un plafond de remboursement.

Exercice 7 — PL-C1-07 (C1, B1.2)

Écoutez le dialogue, puis répondez aux trois questions.

Transcription :

NadiaHave you had a chance to compare the two quotes for the new laptops?
ChrisYes. Corvex is about eight percent cheaper, but their warranty only covers one year. Altamira offers three years, including on-site repairs.
NadiaHmm. Given how often the sales team travels, the repair cover matters more than the price.
ChrisI agree. Shall I ask Altamira whether they'd match part of the price difference?
NadiaGood idea. And copy in Marco from Finance. He'll need to sign it off.

1. What is the main advantage of the Corvex quote?
A. Its lower price
B. Its longer warranty
C. On-site repairs
D. Faster delivery

2. Why does Nadia prefer Altamira?
A. It is cheaper
B. Marco recommends it
C. Its laptops are lighter and easier to carry
D. Repair cover matters for travelling staff

3. What will Chris do?
A. Sign the order without asking Finance
B. Ask Altamira to lower its price
C. Cancel the Corvex quote
D. Meet the sales team

Corrigé

1. A — Its lower price. Corvex est « about eight percent cheaper ». La garantie longue et les réparations sur site sont les atouts d'Altamira, pas de Corvex.
2. D — Repair cover matters for travelling staff. « Given how often the sales team travels, the repair cover matters more than the price. » Marco intervient seulement pour valider la dépense.
3. B — Ask Altamira to lower its price. Il propose de demander à Altamira « whether they'd match part of the price difference » : c'est une négociation. C'est Marco, et non Chris, qui doit signer.

Exercice 8 — PL-C1-08 (C1, B1.2)

Écoutez le message vocal en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

Jamie HartHello Ms Okafor, this is Jamie Hart from Lakeside Conference Centre. I'm calling about your booking for the sales training on the fourteenth. Unfortunately, the projector in the Garden Suite has broken, and the replacement won't arrive in time.
Jamie HartWe can move your group to the Riverside Room, which is slightly bigger and has a built-in screen, at no extra cost.
Jamie HartThe only difference is that lunch would be served in the main restaurant rather than in the room. If that's acceptable, could you confirm by email before Wednesday? Otherwise, I'll call you on Thursday to discuss other options.

1. What is the problem with the booking?
A. A piece of equipment is broken
B. The room is double-booked
C. The training date has changed
D. The centre is closing for repairs

2. What does Jamie ask Ms Okafor to do?
A. Pay an extra fee
B. Call him back before Thursday
C. Confirm the change by email
D. Choose a lunch menu

Corrigé

1. A — A piece of equipment is broken. « The projector in the Garden Suite has broken » : un équipement est en panne. La date du 14 est rappelée, mais elle ne change pas.
2. C — Confirm the change by email. « Could you confirm by email before Wednesday? » C'est Jamie qui rappellera jeudi si elle ne répond pas ; et le changement est « at no extra cost ».

Exercice 9 — PL-C1-09 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez la conversation en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

OwenThanks for joining, Clara. I wanted to talk about the CRM rollout. We're now about three weeks behind schedule.
ClaraI've seen the report. Is it still the data migration?
OwenPartly, but the migration itself is fine now. The real issue is that the sales teams haven't been trained, and we can't go live until they have.
ClaraWhy hasn't the training started? It was planned for September.
OwenThe external trainer pulled out at short notice, and finding a replacement took longer than expected.
ClaraOK. So what are the options?
OwenEither we wait for the new trainer, who's available from the twentieth, or we use two of our own power users to run shorter sessions next week.
ClaraInternal sessions would be quicker, but I'm worried about quality. These are our biggest accounts.
OwenWe could do both: internal sessions now for the basics, and the external trainer later for the advanced features.
ClaraThat sounds reasonable, provided the power users get some relief from their normal targets. Put it in writing and I'll approve it.

1. What is now the main cause of the delay?
A. Continuing problems with the data migration
B. A cut in the project budget
C. A bug in the new software
D. The sales teams have not been trained

2. On what condition will Clara approve the plan?
A. The external trainer starts immediately
B. The total cost goes down
C. The sales teams agree to it
D. The power users' targets are reduced

Corrigé

1. D — The sales teams have not been trained. Owen précise que la migration « is fine now » et que « the real issue is that the sales teams haven't been trained ». La migration est le piège : c'était l'ancien problème.
2. D — The power users' targets are reduced. « Provided the power users get some relief from their normal targets » : « provided » introduit la condition. Le formateur externe n'interviendra que plus tard.

Exercice 10 — PL-C1-10 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez l'annonce en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

Head of OperationsGood afternoon. As many of you know, our lease at the Kingsgate site ends next June. After looking at several options, the board has decided not to renew it.
Head of OperationsInstead, the customer service and finance teams will move to our Easton building, which has been partly empty since the warehouse was automated.
Head of OperationsWe know this will mean a longer commute for some of you. To help, we'll run a free shuttle bus from Kingsgate station for the first twelve months, and anyone who'd prefer to work from home two days a week can now request it through their manager.
Head of OperationsWe'll also hold drop-in sessions next week to answer individual questions.

1. Why are the two teams moving?
A. The current lease is not being renewed
B. The Kingsgate building has been sold to another firm
C. The teams have grown too large
D. The warehouse needs more staff

2. What is offered to help employees?
A. A salary increase
B. Free parking at Easton
C. A temporary transport service
D. Full-time home working for everyone

Corrigé

1. A — The current lease is not being renewed. « The board has decided not to renew it » (le bail). L'entrepôt est cité pour expliquer pourquoi Easton a de la place, pas comme motif du déménagement.
2. C — A temporary transport service. La navette gratuite pendant douze mois est un service de transport temporaire. Le télétravail proposé est de deux jours par semaine, pas à temps plein.

Exercice 11 — PL-C1-11 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez la négociation en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

IngridRafael, I've read your letter about the eleven percent increase. Frankly, that's going to be very hard to justify internally.
RafaelI understand. But our energy costs have nearly doubled, and we've absorbed them for over a year.
IngridI appreciate that, but our contract only allows one price review a year, and we had one in March.
RafaelTrue, though there's a clause covering exceptional cost changes. Our legal team believes this qualifies.
IngridLet's not go down the legal route. What if we accepted a smaller increase now, say five percent, and reviewed it again in six months?
RafaelFive is too low for us. Could you live with seven, if we extended your payment terms from thirty to sixty days?
IngridThat would help our cash flow, I admit. But in return I'd need that rate guaranteed for at least two years.
RafaelI'll have to check with my director, but I think we can work with that.

1. How does Rafael justify the price increase?
A. His company's energy costs have risen sharply
B. Ingrid's company is ordering more than before
C. The contract was signed too long ago
D. A competitor has raised its prices

2. What does Ingrid ask for in exchange for accepting seven percent?
A. Faster deliveries
B. Payment within thirty days
C. A further five percent discount next year
D. A two-year guarantee on the new price

Corrigé

1. A — His company's energy costs have risen sharply. « Our energy costs have nearly doubled » : la hausse des coûts énergétiques est son argument. Il évoque aussi une clause contractuelle, mais pas l'ancienneté du contrat.
2. D — A two-year guarantee on the new price. « I'd need that rate guaranteed for at least two years. » Le passage de 30 à 60 jours de paiement est la concession de Rafael, pas la demande d'Ingrid.

Exercice 12 — PL-C1-12 (C1, B2.2)

Écoutez l'extrait de podcast économique en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

PresenterTurning to the plant-based food sector, the headline figures look encouraging: sales rose by fourteen percent last year. But that number hides a more complicated picture.
PresenterMost of the growth came from just two categories, oat drinks and meat-free burgers, while sales of plant-based ready meals actually fell.
PresenterThe analysts I spoke to were divided. Some see the slowdown as a natural correction after years of hype.
PresenterOthers argue that price is the real issue: plant-based products still cost around thirty percent more than their conventional equivalents, and in a tight economy, many shoppers simply aren't willing to pay that premium.

1. What does the presenter suggest about the fourteen percent figure?
A. It was lower than expected
B. It hides uneven results across categories
C. It mainly reflects strong ready-meal sales
D. It was calculated incorrectly

2. According to some analysts, what is the main obstacle to growth?
A. A lack of product variety
B. Consumers' concerns about health and additives
C. Poor marketing campaigns
D. Higher prices than conventional food

Corrigé

1. B — It hides uneven results across categories. « That number hides a more complicated picture » : la croissance vient de deux catégories seulement. Les plats préparés ont au contraire reculé.
2. D — Higher prices than conventional food. « Price is the real issue… around thirty percent more ». L'idée de « correction after years of hype » est l'avis de l'autre groupe d'analystes.

Exercice 13 — PL-C1-13 (C1, C1.1)

Écoutez l'entretien en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

HelenSo, Marcus, the engagement survey results for your department came back. Overall they're decent, but one thing stood out: people feel decisions are made without them.
MarcusI'm a bit surprised, to be honest. I hold a team meeting every Monday.
HelenYes, and people mentioned that. The point seems to be that by the time something reaches the Monday meeting, it's already been settled. They feel informed rather than consulted.
MarcusFair enough. I suppose I've been trying to shield them from the endless back-and-forth with senior management.
HelenThat's understandable, and nobody doubts your intentions. But there may be a middle ground. You don't need to involve everyone in everything.
MarcusWhat did you have in mind?
HelenPerhaps flag upcoming decisions a week in advance and invite input on the ones that directly affect their work. And be explicit about which decisions are genuinely open and which aren't.
MarcusI can see that working. Although I'd have to be careful it doesn't bog everything down.

1. What is the real issue raised by the survey?
A. Marcus holds too few meetings
B. Senior management ignores the department
C. Staff disagree with most decisions
D. Staff feel they are told, not asked

2. What reservation does Marcus express about Helen's suggestion?
A. It could slow decision-making down
B. It might annoy senior management
C. His team won't be interested in giving input
D. It goes against company policy

Corrigé

1. D — Staff feel they are told, not asked. « They feel informed rather than consulted » : on les informe, on ne les consulte pas. Les réunions existent bien (chaque lundi), donc leur nombre n'est pas en cause.
2. A — It could slow decision-making down. « Bog everything down » signifie enliser, ralentir. Il ne dit pas que la direction s'y opposerait : il parlait d'elle seulement pour expliquer son attitude passée.

Exercice 14 — PL-C1-14 (C1, C1.1)

Écoutez l'extrait de conférence en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

SpeakerThere's a tendency in these debates to treat productivity as if it were a single, easily measurable quantity. It isn't.
SpeakerWhen companies tell us remote staff are more productive, what they've usually measured is output on well-defined, individual tasks, which is precisely the kind of work that benefits from fewer interruptions.
SpeakerWhat those measures tend to miss is the slower, more diffuse stuff: the junior colleague who learns how to handle a difficult client by overhearing a call, or the idea that emerges from a conversation in the corridor.
SpeakerNone of that shows up in this quarter's figures, but you'd be unwise to assume it doesn't show up eventually, usually in the form of a weaker talent pipeline.

1. What is the speaker's criticism of claims about remote productivity?
A. They exaggerate the cost of offices
B. They ignore employee wellbeing
C. They only measure narrow individual tasks
D. They are based on too small a sample of companies

2. What long-term risk does the speaker imply?
A. Less effective development of junior staff
B. Higher office costs
C. More conflict between remote and office teams
D. Lower results this quarter

Corrigé

1. C — They only measure narrow individual tasks. Elle explique que l'on mesure « output on well-defined, individual tasks », un type de travail favorisé par le calme. Elle ne parle ni de coûts ni de taille d'échantillon.
2. A — Less effective development of junior staff. « A weaker talent pipeline » renvoie à l'apprentissage informel des juniors. Elle dit justement que l'effet n'apparaît pas dans les chiffres du trimestre.

Exercice 15 — PL-C1-15 (C1, C1.2)

Écoutez l'échange entre deux dirigeants, en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

VictorOn paper, buying Delmar Analytics makes sense. Their client base complements ours almost perfectly, and the price is, if anything, on the low side.
NaomiWhich is precisely what makes me uneasy. Companies don't usually sell below value unless there's something they'd rather we didn't look at too closely.
VictorDue diligence hasn't flagged anything major. There's the pending dispute with their former co-founder, but our lawyers think the exposure is limited.
NaomiLimited according to whom, though? And based on what?
VictorOur lawyers. Although, admittedly, they've only seen what Delmar chose to disclose.
NaomiThen I'm not prepared to sign off on the current terms. I'm not saying we walk away, but I'd want part of the price held back until the dispute is settled.
VictorAn escrow arrangement. They'll resist it, but it's hardly an unusual request in a deal like this.
NaomiAnd if they refuse outright, that tells us something too, doesn't it?
VictorIt does. I'll put it to their advisers this week and see how they react.

1. Why is Naomi suspicious of the deal?
A. The two client bases overlap too much
B. The asking price seems unusually low
C. Due diligence revealed serious problems
D. Victor has a conflict of interest

2. What does Naomi imply about a possible refusal by Delmar?
A. It would end the negotiations at once
B. It would be a normal negotiating tactic
C. It would force them to raise their asking price
D. It would suggest a bigger risk than claimed

Corrigé

1. B — The asking price seems unusually low. Elle réagit à « the price is on the low side » : une vente sous la valeur cache souvent quelque chose. L'audit, lui, « hasn't flagged anything major ».
2. D — It would suggest a bigger risk than claimed. « That tells us something too » : un refus révélerait que le litige est plus risqué qu'annoncé. Victor juge la demande banale, mais pas le refus.

Exercice 16 — PL-C1-16 (C1, C1.2)

Écoutez le commentaire économique en deux parties. Répondez à une question après chaque partie.

Transcription :

CommentatorIt has become fashionable to speak of reshoring as though bringing production home were simply a matter of political will. The reality is rather less obliging.
CommentatorA firm can relocate a factory in eighteen months; rebuilding the dense web of specialist suppliers, toolmakers and skilled technicians that once surrounded it can take a generation, if it happens at all.
CommentatorNone of which is to dismiss the case for greater resilience. The pandemic exposed genuine vulnerabilities. But resilience and self-sufficiency are not the same thing.
CommentatorFor most firms, the more realistic, and arguably more robust, strategy is diversification: spreading suppliers across several regions so that no single disruption can bring the whole operation to a halt.

1. What point does the commentator make about reshoring?
A. It is mainly blocked by political opposition at home
B. It is faster than most firms believe
C. Rebuilding the supplier network is the hardest part
D. It always reduces production costs

2. What strategy does the commentator recommend?
A. Spreading sourcing across several regions
B. Complete self-sufficiency
C. Relying on a single trusted supplier nearby
D. Moving all production back home

Corrigé

1. C — Rebuilding the supplier network is the hardest part. L'usine se déplace en 18 mois, mais le tissu de fournisseurs et de techniciens peut prendre « a generation ». Il conteste justement l'idée que tout dépend de la volonté politique.
2. A — Spreading sourcing across several regions. « Diversification: spreading suppliers across several regions ». Il distingue explicitement la résilience de l'autosuffisance (« not the same thing »).

Exercice 17 — PL-C1-17 (C1, A2.2)

Écoutez le message et notez les informations demandées (chiffres ou un seul mot).

Transcription :

Sam PorterHello, this is Sam Porter from Greenfield Office Supplies. I'm calling about your order. The order number is four, seven, two, nine. We'll deliver it on Tuesday. If you have any questions, please call me on extension three one five. Thank you.

1. Order number:

2. Delivery day:

3. Sam's extension number:

Corrigé

1. 4729 / 4 7 2 9 / 4-7-2-9. Le numéro est épelé chiffre par chiffre : four, seven, two, nine = 4729.
2. Tuesday / tuesday / on Tuesday. « We'll deliver it on Tuesday » : la livraison a lieu mardi.
3. 315 / 3 1 5 / three one five. « Extension three one five » = poste 315.

Exercice 18 — PL-C1-18 (C1, B1.2)

Écoutez l'annonce et notez les informations demandées (réponse courte).

Transcription :

HR CoordinatorHi everyone, a quick update on the induction day for new recruits. It's now on the ninth of May, not the second, and it'll start at half past eight in the Atlas Room on the third floor. Please bring a copy of your signed contract and your bank details. Lunch will be provided.

1. New date of the induction day:

2. Start time:

3. Name of the room:

Corrigé

1. 9 May / 9th May / May 9 / May 9th / the ninth of May / ninth of May / 9/5 / 09/05. « It's now on the ninth of May, not the second » : le 9 mai remplace le 2 mai.
2. 8:30 / 8.30 / 08:30 / 8h30 / half past eight / 8:30 am / 8.30 am. « Half past eight » = 8 h 30.
3. Atlas / Atlas Room / the Atlas Room / atlas. La salle s'appelle « the Atlas Room », au troisième étage.

Exercice 19 — PL-C1-19 (C1, B2.1)

Écoutez l'échange et notez les informations demandées (chiffre ou réponse courte).

Transcription :

ElenaHow did the Nordic region do in the third quarter?
JonasBetter than forecast. Revenue reached two point four million euros, up eighteen percent on last year, mainly thanks to the new subscription model.
ElenaAnd the churn rate?
JonasDown to six percent, from nine. That's the lowest we've ever had.

1. Revenue in the third quarter (in millions of euros):

2. Increase compared with last year (%):

3. Current churn rate (%):

Corrigé

1. 2.4 / 2,4 / 2.4 million / 2.4 million euros / €2.4 million / 2.4m. « Two point four million euros » = 2,4 millions d'euros.
2. 18 / 18% / 18 % / eighteen / 18 percent. « Up eighteen percent on last year » : hausse de 18 %.
3. 6 / 6% / 6 % / six / 6 percent. Le taux d'attrition est passé de 9 % à 6 % ; la valeur actuelle est 6 %.

Exercice 20 — PL-C1-20 (C1, C1.1)

Écoutez l'annonce de conformité et notez les informations demandées (chiffre ou réponse courte).

Transcription :

Compliance OfficerFollowing the recent audit, we're tightening our policy on supplier gifts and hospitality. With immediate effect, staff may accept hospitality worth no more than fifty pounds per occasion, and anything above twenty pounds must be logged in the gifts register within five working days. Gifts from suppliers currently involved in a tender are prohibited outright, regardless of value.

1. Maximum value of hospitality per occasion (£):

2. Value above which a gift must be logged (£):

3. Deadline for logging it (in working days):

Corrigé

1. 50 / £50 / 50 pounds / fifty / fifty pounds. « No more than fifty pounds per occasion » : 50 £ au maximum.
2. 20 / £20 / 20 pounds / twenty / twenty pounds. « Anything above twenty pounds must be logged » : au-delà de 20 £, déclaration obligatoire.
3. 5 / five / 5 days / five days / 5 working days / five working days. « Within five working days » : sous cinq jours ouvrés.

sections.title: C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais
sections.contentHtml:
Exercice 1 — PL-C2-01 (C2, A2.1)

Lisez l'avis, puis répondez aux questions.

NOTICE – STAFF CAR PARK

From Monday 3 June, the staff car park will be closed for repairs for two weeks. Please park in the visitors' car park on Mill Road. It is five minutes from the main entrance, and your parking card will work there. Please do not park on the street. If you have any questions, contact Facilities on extension 220.

1. Why is the staff car park closing?
A. For repairs
B. For a staff event
C. Because it is full
D. Because of new parking cards

2. What should staff do during the two weeks?
A. Use the car park on Mill Road
B. Buy a new parking card at reception
C. Park on the street
D. Work from home

Corrigé

1. A — For repairs. « Closed for repairs » : fermé pour travaux. Les cartes de stationnement sont mentionnées, mais elles restent valables.
2. A — Use the car park on Mill Road. « Please park in the visitors' car park on Mill Road. » Se garer dans la rue est explicitement interdit (« do not park on the street »).

Exercice 2 — PL-C2-02 (C2, A2.1)

Lisez le courriel, puis répondez aux questions.

From: Anna Berg
To: All staff, Kestrel Design
Subject: Team lunch on Friday

Hi everyone,

To say thank you for your hard work this month, we're having a team lunch this Friday at 12:30 at Luigi's, the Italian restaurant opposite the office. The company will pay. Please tell me by Wednesday if you can come and if you have any food allergies.

Thanks,
Anna

1. What is the email about?
A. A training day
B. A free meal for the team
C. A new client from a restaurant
D. A change of office

2. What must staff do by Wednesday?
A. Pay for the lunch
B. Book a table
C. Choose a restaurant for Friday
D. Tell Anna if they are coming

Corrigé

1. B — A free meal for the team. Il s'agit d'un déjeuner d'équipe offert (« The company will pay »). Le restaurant est un lieu, pas un client.
2. D — Tell Anna if they are coming. « Please tell me by Wednesday if you can come » : répondre à Anna. Le repas est payé par l'entreprise et le restaurant est déjà choisi.

Exercice 3 — PL-C2-03 (C2, A2.2)

Lisez la note de service, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

MEMO
To: Warehouse staff
From: Paul Dunne, Site Manager
Date: 14 October
Re: New working hours

From 1 November, the warehouse will open one hour earlier, at 6 a.m., because we now receive more deliveries in the morning. The morning shift will finish at 2 p.m. instead of 3 p.m. The afternoon shift will not change. If the new hours are a problem for you, please speak to your team leader before 25 October.

1. Why are the opening hours changing?
A. More deliveries arrive in the morning
B. Staff asked for shorter morning shifts
C. The warehouse is moving
D. There is a new team leader

2. Which staff are affected by the change?
A. Only the afternoon shift
B. Only team leaders
C. Both shifts
D. Only the morning shift

3. What should staff do if the new hours are a problem?
A. Write to Paul Dunne before 25 October
B. Change to another shift
C. Talk to their team leader
D. Wait until 1 November

Corrigé

1. A — More deliveries arrive in the morning. « Because we now receive more deliveries in the morning. » Aucune demande du personnel n'est évoquée.
2. D — Only the morning shift. Seule l'équipe du matin change d'horaires ; « the afternoon shift will not change ».
3. C — Talk to their team leader. « Please speak to your team leader before 25 October. » Paul Dunne signe la note, mais ce n'est pas lui qu'il faut contacter.

Exercice 4 — PL-C2-04 (C2, A2.2)

Lisez l'offre d'emploi, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

JOB OPPORTUNITY – Customer Service Assistant

Harbour Travel is looking for a friendly Customer Service Assistant to join our team in Bristol. You will answer phone calls and emails from customers, help them change their bookings and solve simple problems. You need good English and basic computer skills. Experience in travel is useful but not necessary, as we give full training. The job is part-time: Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. To apply, send your CV to jobs@harbourtravel.example by 30 April.

1. What is one task in this job?
A. Selling holidays in a shop
B. Helping customers change their bookings
C. Training new staff in the Bristol office
D. Organising company trips

2. What does the advert say about experience in travel?
A. At least two years are required
B. Only travel experience is accepted
C. It is not essential
D. It must be in Bristol

3. How many days a week is the job?
A. Three
B. Four
C. Five
D. Six

Corrigé

1. B — Helping customers change their bookings. « Help them change their bookings. » La formation est donnée au nouvel employé ; il n'en assure pas.
2. C — It is not essential. « Useful but not necessary » : utile mais pas obligatoire, car une formation complète est prévue.
3. B — Four. Du lundi au jeudi = quatre jours. Le mot « part-time » peut faire penser à trois jours, mais le texte précise les jours.

Exercice 5 — PL-C2-05 (C2, B1.1)

Lisez le courriel, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

From: Rachel Moore, Office Manager
To: Kim Tanaka
Subject: Your first day – Monday 6 May

Dear Kim,

We're delighted that you're joining Tidewell Insurance as a Claims Assistant. I'm writing to give you some information about your first day.

Please arrive at 9:15 rather than 9:00, as the security team need to take your photo for your ID badge first. Ask for me at reception on the ground floor. In the morning, you'll have an introduction to our systems with Liam from IT. After lunch, you'll meet your manager, Gary Holt, who'll explain your main responsibilities.

You don't need to bring a laptop, but please bring your passport or ID card so that we can complete your file.

I look forward to meeting you.

Best regards,
Rachel

1. Why should Kim arrive at 9:15?
A. Reception opens at 9:15
B. Gary Holt is busy with meetings until then
C. The IT introduction starts at 9:15
D. Security need to take her badge photo

2. Who will Kim meet in the afternoon?
A. Rachel Moore
B. Liam from IT
C. Her manager
D. The security team

3. What must Kim bring?
A. A laptop
B. An identity document
C. A photo
D. A copy of her contract

Corrigé

1. D — Security need to take her badge photo. « As the security team need to take your photo for your ID badge first. » Rien n'indique l'heure d'ouverture de l'accueil.
2. C — Her manager. « After lunch, you'll meet your manager, Gary Holt. » Liam intervient le matin.
3. B — An identity document. « Please bring your passport or ID card » : une pièce d'identité. L'ordinateur n'est pas nécessaire, et la photo est prise sur place.

Exercice 6 — PL-C2-06 (C2, B1.1)

Lisez l'article de la lettre interne, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Cycle to Work Scheme Now Open

Following requests from many employees, Ardent Pharma is launching a cycle to work scheme this spring. Under the scheme, the company buys a bicycle and safety equipment for you, up to a value of £1,500, and you pay it back in monthly amounts taken from your salary over twelve months. Because the payments are made before tax, the total cost to you is usually 25 to 35 percent lower than buying the bike yourself.

New showers and secure bike storage have also been installed in the basement of Building C. To join, complete the online form on the HR portal before 31 March. Places are limited to 80 employees this year, so early applications are recommended.

1. Why has the company introduced the scheme?
A. To reduce car park costs
B. Because many employees asked for it
C. Because of a new law
D. To win an environmental award this year

2. Why is a bike cheaper through the scheme?
A. The company pays half of the price of the bike
B. The bike shop gives a discount
C. The bikes are second-hand
D. Payments are taken from salary before tax

3. Why are employees advised to apply early?
A. Bike prices will rise after March
B. The storage area is small
C. The number of places is limited
D. The HR portal closes in April

Corrigé

1. B — Because many employees asked for it. « Following requests from many employees » : à la demande du personnel. Le texte ne parle ni de loi ni de prix.
2. D — Payments are taken from salary before tax. « Because the payments are made before tax » : l'économie vient de la fiscalité. L'entreprise avance l'argent mais ne paie pas la moitié.
3. C — The number of places is limited. « Places are limited to 80 employees this year. » Le 31 mars est une date limite, mais aucune hausse de prix n'est annoncée.

Exercice 7 — PL-C2-07 (C2, B1.2)

Lisez le courriel de réclamation, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

From: Martin Feld, Purchasing Manager, Corlan Hotels
To: customer.service@pureline-linen.example
Subject: Order 58321 – incorrect delivery

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about our order no. 58321, which was delivered to our Lyon hotel on 3 September. We ordered 200 white king-size sheets, but we received 200 double sheets, which do not fit our beds. In addition, 15 of the towels in the same delivery were stained.

This is the second time this year that we have had a problem with a delivery, and it is causing us serious difficulties, as a large conference group is arriving on 12 September.

I would therefore be grateful if you could send the correct sheets and replace the damaged towels before 10 September. Please also arrange for the wrong items to be collected at your expense.

If this is not possible, I will have no choice but to cancel the order and look for another supplier.

Yours faithfully,
Martin Feld

1. What was wrong with the sheets?
A. They were stained
B. They were the wrong size
C. They arrived late
D. They were the wrong colour

2. Why is the new delivery date important?
A. The hotel is closing for renovation
B. The hotel has already chosen a new supplier
C. The conference starts on 10 September
D. A large group is arriving soon

3. What will Martin do if the problem is not solved in time?
A. Ask for a discount
B. Keep the double sheets
C. Cancel the order
D. Call the supplier's manager

Corrigé

1. B — They were the wrong size. Des draps « double » au lieu de « king-size » : mauvaise taille. Ce sont les serviettes, pas les draps, qui étaient tachées.
2. D — A large group is arriving soon. « A large conference group is arriving on 12 September. » Le 10 septembre est la date limite de livraison, pas la date d'arrivée du groupe.
3. C — Cancel the order. « I will have no choice but to cancel the order and look for another supplier. » Aucune remise n'est demandée.

Exercice 8 — PL-C2-08 (C2, B1.2)

Lisez l'article, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Four-Day Week Trial: First Results

Six months ago, the marketing department at Selwyn Software began a trial in which staff worked four days a week for the same salary, on condition that their results did not fall. The first results, published last week, are generally positive.

According to the report, the team completed 96 percent of their planned projects, compared with 94 percent in the same period last year. Sick days fell by almost a third, and in an anonymous survey, 88 percent of the team said they felt less stressed.

However, the trial has not been without problems. Clients sometimes complained that they could not reach anyone on Fridays, and two team leaders said they were working extra hours from home to keep up. Management has decided to continue the trial for another six months, but with a rota so that the office is always staffed from Monday to Friday.

1. What was the condition of the trial?
A. Results had to stay at the same level
B. Staff had to work longer hours each day
C. Salaries were slightly reduced
D. Only volunteers could take part

2. Which result of the trial is mentioned?
A. More projects were cancelled
B. Sick days decreased
C. Clients were more satisfied
D. Salaries increased

3. How will the trial change?
A. It will end in six months
B. It will include all departments
C. Staff will take different days off
D. Team leaders will go back to five days

Corrigé

1. A — Results had to stay at the same level. « On condition that their results did not fall. » Le salaire restait le même (« for the same salary »).
2. B — Sick days decreased. « Sick days fell by almost a third. » Les clients, au contraire, se sont parfois plaints.
3. C — Staff will take different days off. Un roulement (« a rota ») garantit une présence du lundi au vendredi : les jours de repos seront répartis. L'essai est prolongé, pas arrêté.

Exercice 9 — PL-C2-09 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez l'extrait de rapport, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Customer Satisfaction Survey – Summary of Findings

This year's survey was completed by 1,240 customers, a response rate of 31 percent, slightly higher than last year. Overall satisfaction remained stable at 7.8 out of 10.

Delivery speed was once again the area most frequently praised, with 82 percent of respondents rating it as good or excellent. This reflects the investment made in the new regional depot in Leeds, which has reduced average delivery times in the north from four days to two.

By contrast, satisfaction with after-sales support has declined for the second consecutive year, from 7.1 to 6.4. Comments suggest that the main frustration is not the quality of the answers provided but the time it takes to get them: the average waiting time on the support line has risen to 14 minutes. Several customers also noted that they had to explain their problem more than once when they were transferred between agents.

We recommend introducing a callback option and a shared case history so that agents can see previous contacts. Both measures could be implemented within the current budget.

1. How did overall satisfaction change this year?
A. It rose sharply
B. It stayed about the same
C. It fell slightly
D. It fell sharply

2. What explains the positive rating of delivery speed?
A. Faster couriers
B. Fewer orders in the north
C. A new regional depot
D. Lower delivery prices

3. According to customers, what is the main problem with after-sales support?
A. The answers are often wrong
B. The agents are impolite
C. The line is closed at weekends
D. It takes too long to get help

Corrigé

1. B — It stayed about the same. « Remained stable at 7.8 ». C'est le taux de réponse qui a légèrement augmenté, pas la satisfaction.
2. C — A new regional depot. « This reflects the investment made in the new regional depot in Leeds. »
3. D — It takes too long to get help. « Not the quality of the answers… but the time it takes to get them. » Le texte écarte explicitement la qualité des réponses.

Exercice 10 — PL-C2-10 (C2, B2.1)

Lisez le courriel, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

From: Lucia Romano, Events Director, Meridian Pharma
To: Tom Ashby, Sales Manager, Castleview Hotel
Subject: RE: Quotation for annual sales conference

Dear Tom,

Thank you for your quotation for our sales conference on 18-20 March. Your venue was clearly the favourite among the committee members who visited last month, particularly because of the main hall and the quality of the catering.

However, the total of €68,500 is around 12 percent above our budget, and we have received a competitive offer from another hotel in the area. Before we make a final decision, I wanted to see whether there is any flexibility.

In particular, we would like to know whether you could include the audiovisual equipment, currently charged at €4,200, in the room rental. We would also be prepared to reduce the number of breakout rooms from six to four if that would lower the price. On our side, we could confirm the booking by the end of this month and pay a 40 percent deposit, rather than the 25 percent mentioned in your terms.

I would be grateful for your reply by Friday, as the committee meets next Monday.

Kind regards,
Lucia Romano

1. What is the main purpose of Lucia's email?
A. To confirm the booking
B. To complain about the site visit
C. To negotiate a lower price
D. To cancel the conference

2. What does Lucia say about the other hotel?
A. Its catering is better
B. It has made a competitive offer
C. Its main hall is larger
D. The committee preferred it

3. What does Lucia offer in return?
A. An earlier decision and a larger deposit
B. A larger number of guests
C. A longer conference
D. Free publicity for the hotel

Corrigé

1. C — To negotiate a lower price. Le devis dépasse le budget de 12 % et elle cherche « any flexibility » : elle négocie. Elle ne confirme pas encore.
2. B — It has made a competitive offer. « We have received a competitive offer from another hotel. » Le comité a au contraire préféré Castleview.
