3. A — An earlier decision and a larger deposit. Elle propose de confirmer avant la fin du mois et de verser 40 % d'acompte au lieu de 25 %.

Exercice 11 — PL-C2-11 (C2, B2.2)

Lisez l'article, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Hiring for Skills, Not Degrees

A growing number of employers are dropping degree requirements from job advertisements, arguing that what matters is what candidates can do, not where they studied. Supporters say the approach widens the talent pool, improves diversity and reduces staff turnover, since employees hired for proven skills tend to be better matched to their roles.

Yet a recent study by the Fairmont Institute suggests that the shift may be more cosmetic than real. Although the proportion of advertisements without a degree requirement has doubled in five years, the proportion of non-graduates actually hired into those roles has risen by less than four percentage points. In many cases, the researchers found, recruiters continued to filter applications by education informally, or hiring managers simply preferred graduates when faced with two otherwise similar candidates.

The authors argue that removing a line from a job advertisement is the easy part. Genuine change requires redesigning the selection process itself: structured interviews, practical work samples and clear scoring criteria that leave less room for habit and unconscious bias. Companies that had made these deeper changes, the study found, hired non-graduates at three times the rate of those that had not.

1. What do supporters of skills-based hiring claim?
A. It reduces recruitment costs
B. Employees tend to stay longer
C. It speeds up recruitment
D. It attracts more graduates

2. What does the Fairmont study suggest?
A. Few companies have removed degree requirements
B. Non-graduates perform better than graduates
C. Recruiters have stopped checking education
D. Dropping degree requirements has had little real effect on hiring

3. According to the authors, what makes the real difference?
A. Changing how candidates are assessed
B. Advertising jobs more widely
C. Training managers in employment law
D. Offering higher salaries

Corrigé

1. B — Employees tend to stay longer. « Reduces staff turnover » = les salariés restent plus longtemps. Le coût et la rapidité du recrutement ne sont pas évoqués.
2. D — Dropping degree requirements has had little real effect on hiring. « More cosmetic than real » : les annonces ont changé, mais l'embauche de non-diplômés n'a progressé que de moins de 4 points. Les recruteurs continuent au contraire à filtrer sur le diplôme.
3. A — Changing how candidates are assessed. Entretiens structurés, mises en situation, grilles de notation : c'est le processus de sélection qu'il faut revoir. Supprimer une ligne de l'annonce est « the easy part ».

Exercice 12 — PL-C2-12 (C2, B2.2)

Lisez le compte rendu de réunion, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Minutes – Product Steering Committee
Date: 4 February
Present: J. Whitfield (Chair), S. Mensah, L. Grant, P. Novak
Apologies: R. Ito

  1. Launch date of the Aurora app

S. Mensah reported that user testing had revealed a significant number of problems with the payment function on older Android devices. Fixing them would take approximately three weeks. L. Grant argued that delaying the launch would mean missing the spring marketing campaign, for which €120,000 had already been committed. After discussion, the committee agreed to launch on the planned date of 1 March for iOS only, with the Android version following once testing has been completed. Action: L. Grant to inform the agency so that campaign materials can be adjusted.

  1. Pricing

P. Novak presented three pricing options. The committee did not reach agreement. Concerns were raised that the premium tier was not sufficiently differentiated from the standard tier. Action: P. Novak to revise the proposal, including competitor benchmarks, for the next meeting.

  1. AOB

J. Whitfield reminded members that R. Ito will be leaving the company at the end of March. A replacement on the committee will be nominated by the Finance department.

Next meeting: 18 February.

1. Why will the Android version be launched later?
A. The marketing agency was not ready
B. Problems were found with the payment function
C. The budget had been exceeded
D. R. Ito was absent from the meeting

2. What was decided about pricing?
A. The standard tier will be dropped
B. The premium tier will be cheaper
C. A revised proposal will be presented later
D. The third option was approved

3. What can be inferred about R. Ito?
A. R. Ito represents the Finance department on the committee
B. R. Ito chairs the committee
C. R. Ito disagreed with the launch plan
D. R. Ito presented the pricing options

Corrigé

1. B — Problems were found with the payment function. Les tests ont révélé des problèmes de paiement sur les anciens appareils Android. L'agence devra seulement adapter la campagne.
2. C — A revised proposal will be presented later. « The committee did not reach agreement » ; P. Novak présentera une proposition révisée à la prochaine réunion.
3. A — R. Ito represents the Finance department on the committee. Son remplaçant sera désigné par le service Finance : on en déduit que R. Ito y représente la Finance. La présidence revient à J. Whitfield.

Exercice 13 — PL-C2-13 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez l'article, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

When Green Claims Backfire

For much of the past decade, sustainability messaging was treated by many companies as a low-risk, high-reward exercise. A carefully worded commitment to reach net zero by 2050 cost little, generated positive headlines, and was unlikely to be scrutinised until long after the executives who made it had moved on.

That calculation is changing. Regulators in several jurisdictions now require environmental claims to be specific, substantiated and verifiable, and they have begun to fine firms that fall short. Meanwhile, activist investors and campaign groups have become adept at comparing public pledges with what companies actually disclose in their annual accounts, and are quick to publicise any gap.

The result, somewhat paradoxically, has been a rise in what some analysts call greenhushing: companies that are making genuine progress choosing to say less about it, for fear that any imperfection in their data will be seized upon. A survey of 1,200 firms last year found that almost a quarter had deliberately scaled back their sustainability communications, even though their targets remained unchanged.

Some observers welcome this as a healthy correction after years of exaggeration. Others are more concerned. If the companies doing the most are also saying the least, they argue, investors and consumers lose the very information they need to reward good performance, and the pressure on laggards to improve is correspondingly reduced. The challenge for regulators, then, is to deter misleading claims without discouraging honest ones.

1. What does the writer suggest about sustainability claims in the past?
A. They were strictly regulated
B. They carried little risk for those who made them
C. They were mainly made by small firms
D. They were usually accurate

2. What does the term greenhushing refer to?
A. Companies hiding environmental damage
B. Regulators keeping fines confidential
C. Companies that are making progress deliberately communicating less about it
D. Investors ignoring sustainability data

3. What concern do some observers raise?
A. Fines are too low to be effective
B. Consumers no longer care about the environment
C. Companies are abandoning their targets
D. Silence from strong performers weakens the pressure on weaker ones

Corrigé

1. B — They carried little risk for those who made them. « A low-risk, high-reward exercise… unlikely to be scrutinised » : peu de risques pour leurs auteurs. La régulation stricte est récente (« That calculation is changing »).
2. C — Companies that are making progress deliberately communicating less about it. Des entreprises qui progressent réellement « choosing to say less about it ». Il ne s'agit pas de cacher des dégâts, mais de taire de vrais progrès.
3. D — Silence from strong performers weakens the pressure on weaker ones. « The pressure on laggards to improve is correspondingly reduced. » Les objectifs, eux, restent inchangés (« their targets remained unchanged »).

Exercice 14 — PL-C2-14 (C2, C1.1)

Lisez le courriel interne, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

From: Daniel Okoye, Operations Director
To: Executive Committee
Subject: Review of the warehouse automation pilot

Colleagues,

As requested, here is my assessment of the six-month automation pilot at our Tilbury warehouse, ahead of next week's decision on whether to extend it to our other three sites.

The headline figures are, on the face of it, impressive: picking errors fell by 41 percent and throughput rose by 18 percent. I would caution, however, against reading too much into them. The pilot site was selected precisely because it had the most modern building and the most experienced workforce, and it received a level of support from the vendor's engineers that we cannot assume will be available, or affordable, at scale.

More significantly, the projected payback period of three years rests on labour savings that have not yet materialised. Headcount at Tilbury is unchanged, partly because staff have been redeployed to supervise the robots, and partly because the system still requires manual intervention more often than the vendor anticipated.

None of this is an argument for abandoning automation. I remain convinced that it is the right long-term direction. But I would recommend a more cautious next step: extending the pilot to one further site, ideally our oldest one at Corby, where conditions are least favourable. If the results hold there, we will have a far more reliable basis for a group-wide investment of this size.

Daniel

1. Why does Daniel question the headline figures?
A. They were calculated by the vendor
B. The pilot took place in unusually favourable conditions
C. They cover too short a period
D. They contradict staff feedback

2. What does Daniel say about the projected payback period?
A. It depends on labour savings that have not happened yet
B. It has already been achieved
C. It is shorter than expected
D. It has been approved by the committee

3. Why does Daniel suggest Corby for the next stage?
A. It is the cheapest site to equip
B. Its staff have asked for automation
C. A good result there would be more convincing
D. It is closest to the vendor

Corrigé

1. B — The pilot took place in unusually favourable conditions. Le site pilote a été choisi pour son bâtiment moderne, son personnel expérimenté et un fort soutien du fournisseur : conditions non représentatives. La durée n'est pas critiquée.
2. A — It depends on labour savings that have not happened yet. « Rests on labour savings that have not yet materialised » : l'effectif de Tilbury n'a pas baissé.
3. C — A good result there would be more convincing. Corby offre les conditions « least favourable » : si les résultats tiennent là, la preuve sera plus fiable. Ce n'est pas une question de coût.

Exercice 15 — PL-C2-15 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez l'article d'opinion, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

The Subscription Trap

There was a time, not so long ago, when converting a product into a subscription was regarded as the closest thing in business to a free lunch. Recurring revenue was predictable, investors rewarded it with generous valuations, and customers, lulled by modest monthly fees, seemed scarcely to notice what they were paying in aggregate.

That consensus is fraying. Churn rates across consumer subscription services have climbed steadily, and a growing share of customers now cancel and re-subscribe according to whatever they happen to want that month, a behaviour the industry has rather ruefully christened serial churning. What was meant to be a long-term relationship has, for many users, become a series of short-term transactions, with the added cost to the provider of re-acquiring the same customer several times a year.

Business-to-business software, long assumed to be immune, is not faring much better. Finance departments under pressure to cut costs have started auditing the dozens of tools their companies subscribe to, often discovering licences that nobody has used in months. Vendors that once took renewals for granted are finding themselves in negotiations they had not prepared for.

It would be premature to declare the model dead. For products that are genuinely used every day, a subscription remains a perfectly sensible arrangement for both sides. The difficulty lies with the many firms that adopted it not because it suited their product but because it suited their valuation. For them, the coming years are likely to involve some uncomfortable rethinking, and perhaps a quiet return to the old-fashioned practice of simply selling things.

1. Why were subscriptions initially so attractive to companies?
A. Customers explicitly asked for them
B. They were cheaper to operate
C. Regulators encouraged them
D. They generated predictable income that investors rewarded

2. What does serial churning describe?
A. Customers switching permanently to a competitor
B. Customers repeatedly cancelling and re-subscribing
C. Providers changing their prices every month
D. Companies cancelling unused software licences

3. What is the writer's overall view of the subscription model?
A. It is no longer viable for any business
B. It works for business software but not for consumers
C. It suits some products, but many firms adopted it for the wrong reasons
D. It should be restricted by law

Corrigé

1. D — They generated predictable income that investors rewarded. « Recurring revenue was predictable, investors rewarded it with generous valuations. » Les clients ne les réclamaient pas : ils « remarquaient à peine » ce qu'ils payaient.
2. B — Customers repeatedly cancelling and re-subscribing. « Cancel and re-subscribe according to whatever they happen to want that month ». Les licences inutilisées concernent le B2B, un autre paragraphe.
3. C — It suits some products, but many firms adopted it for the wrong reasons. « It would be premature to declare the model dead » : il reste pertinent pour les produits utilisés tous les jours, mais beaucoup l'ont adopté « because it suited their valuation ». Le B2B est dit en difficulté lui aussi.

Exercice 16 — PL-C2-16 (C2, C1.2)

Lisez la lettre de la présidente du conseil d'administration, puis répondez aux questions dans l'ordre du texte.

Letter from the Chair – Annual Report

Dear Shareholders,

It would be disingenuous to describe the past year as anything other than difficult. Revenue fell by 6 percent, and although the decline was concentrated in our European construction division, its effects were felt across the group. The board does not believe that external conditions alone account for this performance. Rising interest rates certainly dampened demand, but several of our competitors weathered the same environment considerably better.

In our view, the underlying problem has been one of focus. Over the past decade, the group expanded into a number of adjacent markets, some of which have delivered value while others, frankly, have absorbed management attention out of all proportion to their contribution. The decision announced in September to divest our facilities management business should be understood in that light: it was profitable, but it was never going to be central to what we do best.

You will also have noted the change of leadership. Mark Ellison stepped down as Chief Executive in June after eleven years, and the board is grateful for his contribution, not least in building the infrastructure division into the group's most reliable source of earnings. His successor, Farah Qureshi, brings extensive experience of operational turnaround, which is precisely what the coming period demands.

We have decided to maintain the dividend at last year's level. Some will argue that a cut would have been more prudent; we took the view that the group's balance sheet remains robust and that confidence in our long-term prospects is warranted. That said, I should be clear that this is not a commitment for future years, which will depend on the progress of the turnaround plan.

Yours faithfully,
Eleanor Vance, Chair

1. How does the Chair explain the poor performance?
A. It was entirely caused by rising interest rates
B. The group's own lack of strategic focus was partly to blame
C. Competitors used unfair practices
D. The former Chief Executive mismanaged the construction division

2. Why was the facilities management business sold?
A. It did not fit the group's core strengths
B. It was making a loss
C. A competitor made an attractive offer
D. The new Chief Executive requested it

3. What does the Chair imply about future dividends?
A. They will definitely increase
B. They will be cut next year
C. They are not guaranteed
D. They will be paid in shares

Corrigé

1. B — The group's own lack of strategic focus was partly to blame. « External conditions alone » ne suffisent pas, et « the underlying problem has been one of focus ». Les taux d'intérêt ont joué, mais pas « entirely ».
2. A — It did not fit the group's core strengths. « It was profitable, but it was never going to be central to what we do best. » Elle était donc rentable : le piège est « making a loss ».
3. C — They are not guaranteed. « This is not a commitment for future years » : le dividende futur dépendra du plan de redressement. Rien n'annonce une baisse certaine.

Exercice 17 — PL-GV-02 (C2, A2.1)

Choisissez le mot qui convient pour compléter la présentation de l'entreprise.

Our company [1] _____ office furniture. We have 50 [2] _____ who work in the factory and in the office. Our biggest [3] _____ are schools and hospitals: they buy our desks and chairs.

[1] spends / borrows / sells / earns

[2] customers / employees / suppliers / products

[3] customers / workers / colleagues / bosses

Corrigé

[1] sells. L'entreprise vend (« sells ») des meubles. « Earns » (gagner) s'emploie pour de l'argent, pas pour un produit.
[2] employees. Des personnes « who work in the factory » sont des salariés (« employees »), pas des clients.
[3] customers. Les écoles « buy our desks » : ce sont des clients (« customers »).

Exercice 18 — PL-GV-04 (C2, A2.2)

Choisissez le mot qui complète correctement les consignes affichées à l'accueil.

VISITOR INFORMATION
Please [1] _____ the form and give it to reception. All visitors must [2] _____ in and wear a badge at all times. Mobile phones must be switched [3] _____ in the laboratory.

[1] fill up / full in / make up / fill in

[2] sing / signal / sign / write

[3] out / off / down / away

Corrigé

[1] fill in. On remplit un formulaire : « fill in a form ». « Fill up » signifie remplir un récipient.
[2] sign. « Sign in » = signer le registre d'entrée. Attention au faux ami visuel « sing » (chanter).
[3] off. « Switch off » = éteindre un appareil. « Switch out » n'existe pas dans ce sens.

Exercice 19 — PL-GV-06 (C2, B1.1)

Choisissez le mot qui complète correctement l'extrait de la lettre d'information.

We are pleased to [1] _____ that our sales increased by 12% last year. This success is largely [2] _____ to our new online shop. Next year, we [3] _____ to open two new stores in Manchester and Glasgow.

[1] announce / advertise / pronounce / inform

[2] thanks / because / result / due

[3] consider / think / plan / look forward

Corrigé

[1] announce. « Announce that… » = annoncer une nouvelle. « Inform » exige un complément de personne (« inform you that »).
[2] due. « Due to » = grâce à / dû à. « Thanks » s'écrirait « thanks to » mais pas après « is largely ».
[3] plan. « Plan to + verbe » = prévoir de. « Consider » est suivi de -ing, et « look forward to » aussi.

Exercice 20 — PL-GV-08 (C2, B1.2)

Choisissez le mot qui convient dans ce message sur une réunion.

The project meeting has been [1] _____ until next week because the director is ill. Please [2] _____ the agenda before the meeting and send me any [3] _____ for changes. The [4] _____ will be circulated to everyone afterwards.

[1] cancelled / postponed / put on / delayed off

[2] review / reply / remind / resume

[3] advices / informations / councils / suggestions

[4] hours / seconds / minutes / agendas

Corrigé

[1] postponed. « Postponed until next week » = reportée. « Cancelled » (annulée) n'est pas compatible avec « until next week ».
[2] review. « Review the agenda » = relire, examiner l'ordre du jour. « Remind » signifie rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un.
[3] suggestions. « Suggestions » est dénombrable. « Advice » et « information » sont indénombrables : jamais de -s.
[4] minutes. Le compte rendu de réunion se dit « the minutes » en anglais professionnel.

Exercice 21 — PL-GV-10 (C2, B2.1)

Choisissez le mot qui convient dans ce point d'avancement de projet.

The project has gone 15% [1] _____ budget, mainly because of unexpected material costs. We will need to cut [2] _____ elsewhere, but certainly not on safety. I suggest we [3] _____ this with the client before it becomes a bigger issue, as their [4] _____ is required before any change to the scope.

[1] under / over / off / out of

[2] corners / edges / angles / costs down

[3] rise / arise / lift / raise

[4] approve / approving / approval / approved

Corrigé

[1] over. « Over budget » = au-delà du budget. « Under budget » dirait l'inverse, ce que contredisent les coûts imprévus.
[2] corners. Expression « cut corners » = rogner (souvent au détriment de la qualité), d'où « not on safety ».
[3] raise. « Raise an issue with someone » = soulever un sujet. « Rise » et « arise » sont intransitifs.
[4] approval. Après le possessif « their », il faut un nom : « their approval ».

Exercice 22 — PL-GV-12 (C2, B2.2)

Choisissez le terme juridique ou commercial qui convient.

The new contract includes a [1] _____ clause allowing either party to end the agreement with 90 days' notice. Payment [2] _____ remain 30 days from the date of invoice. Any [3] _____ arising from the contract will be settled by arbitration. Please note that these terms are [4] _____ to final approval by our legal department.

[1] terminal / termination / ending / finishing

[2] terms / dates / limits / scales

[3] arguments / quarrels / fights / disputes

[4] due / liable / subject / submitted

Corrigé

[1] termination. « Termination clause » = clause de résiliation. « Terminal » est un adjectif sans rapport (terminal, en phase terminale).
[2] terms. « Payment terms » = conditions de paiement, la collocation standard.
[3] disputes. En contexte contractuel on parle de « disputes » (litiges). « Arguments » désigne une dispute verbale ou un raisonnement.
[4] subject. « Subject to approval » = sous réserve d'approbation. « Liable to » signifie susceptible de / passible de.

Exercice 23 — PL-GV-14 (C2, C1.1)

Choisissez le mot qui convient dans cet extrait de presse économique.

The CEO's decision to [1] _____ the restructuring plan came as a surprise, given that she had been its most vocal [2] _____. Analysts suggest she may have been [3] _____ by pressure from major shareholders. Either way, the move has [4] _____ doubt on the company's strategic direction.

[1] shelve / shell / shelter / shift

[2] adversary / advisor / auditor / advocate

[3] swung / swept / swayed / swapped

[4] thrown / cast / laid / drawn

Corrigé

[1] shelve. « Shelve a plan » = mettre un projet au placard, le suspendre. « Shelter » signifie abriter.
[2] advocate. La surprise vient de ce qu'elle en était la plus ardente partisane (« advocate »). « Adversary » rendrait la décision logique, donc pas surprenante.
[3] swayed. « Be swayed by » = être influencé par. « Swung » (balancé) ne s'emploie pas ainsi au passif.
[4] cast. Collocation « cast doubt on » = jeter le doute sur.

Exercice 24 — PL-GV-16 (C2, C1.2)

Choisissez le mot ou l'expression le plus précis dans cet extrait de compte rendu.

The audit report was [1] _____ in its criticism, leaving little room for interpretation. Management's response, by contrast, was [2] _____, committing to nothing specific. Several board members expressed [3] _____ at what they saw as an attempt to [4] _____ the issue. The episode has left the CEO's credibility [5] _____.

[1] unequivocal / ambivalent / tentative / unanimous

[2] forthright / decisive / outspoken / noncommittal

[3] dismal / dismissal / dismay / disarray

[4] sidetrack / sidestep / sideline / sideswipe

[5] in tatters / in tandem / in check / in shape

Corrigé

[1] unequivocal. « Leaving little room for interpretation » = sans équivoque, « unequivocal ». « Ambivalent » et « tentative » disent le contraire.
[2] noncommittal. « Committing to nothing specific » = évasif, « noncommittal ». « Forthright » (franc) contredit la suite.
[3] dismay. « Express dismay at » = exprimer sa consternation face à. « Dismal » est un adjectif (lugubre).
[4] sidestep. « Sidestep an issue » = esquiver une question. « Sideline » signifie mettre quelqu'un sur la touche.
[5] in tatters. « Credibility in tatters » = crédibilité en lambeaux. « In check » signifie « maîtrisé ».

sections.title: C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais
sections.contentHtml:
Exercice 1 — PL-C3-01 (C3, B1.1)

Lisez d'abord le texte en silence (30 secondes), puis lisez-le à voix haute, clairement et à un rythme naturel. Cet exercice est corrigé par le formateur.

Welcome to Northgate Logistics. Our company was founded in 2009, and today we employ more than four hundred people in six countries. We specialise in temperature-controlled transport for food and medical products. Last year, we delivered over two million parcels, and ninety-eight percent of them arrived on time. This year, we are investing in electric vehicles and a new warehouse near Rotterdam. Our aim is simple: to deliver faster, safer and cleaner than ever before.

Corrigé

Points de prononciation : Nombres (2009 = « twenty oh nine », four hundred, ninety-eight percent) ; accent de mot (« temperature-controlled », « specialise », « investing ») ; terminaisons -ed de « founded » (/ɪd/) et « delivered » (/d/) ; pause avant les deux-points et intonation descendante sur la dernière phrase.

Exercice 2 — PL-C3-02 (C3, B1.2)

Écoutez chaque phrase une fois, puis répétez-la exactement, avec la même intonation. Les phrases sont de plus en plus longues (niveau A2 à B2). Exercice corrigé par le formateur.

  1. Please call me back.
  2. The meeting starts at ten.
  3. Could you send me the report by Friday?
  4. We've moved the deadline to the end of next month.
  5. If the shipment is delayed again, we'll have to inform the client immediately.
  6. Although sales rose in the second quarter, our margins were affected by higher transport costs.

Corrigé

Répéter chaque phrase en respectant le rythme, l’accentuation et la liaison ; s’enregistrer et comparer au modèle.

Exercice 3 — PL-C3-03 (C3, A2.2)

Préparez-vous 30 secondes, puis répondez à voix haute pendant 45 secondes. Réponse corrigée par le formateur.

Question : Please introduce yourself. Tell us your name, what you do, where you work and what you do on a typical working day. (préparation 30 s, réponse 45 s)

Langue utile : My name is… / I'm… · I work as a… at… · I'm in charge of… · On a typical day, I… · First… Then… In the afternoon… · I like my job because…

Corrigé

Critères : Donne les informations demandées : nom, poste, lieu de travail, activités d'une journée type ; Utilise le présent simple correctement (I work, I answer, I meet) ; Phrases simples mais complètes, reliées par and, but, then ; Prononciation compréhensible sans effort excessif ; Parle pendant au moins 30 secondes sans longues pauses
Réponse modèle : Hello, my name is Karim Benali. I'm a sales assistant at Delta Home, a company that sells kitchen equipment. I work in our office in Lille. On a typical day, I start at half past eight. First, I read my emails and answer questions from customers. Then I prepare quotes and send them to our clients. In the afternoon, I often call customers to check their orders. I like my job because I speak to a lot of different people.

Exercice 4 — PL-C3-04 (C3, B1.2)

Préparez-vous 30 secondes, puis répondez à voix haute pendant 60 secondes. Réponse corrigée par le formateur.

Question : Describe a problem you had at work. What happened, what did you do to solve it, and what did you learn from it? (préparation 30 s, réponse 60 s)

Langue utile : I was responsible for… · The problem was that… · At first, I… · So I decided to… · In the end, … · What I learned is that…

Corrigé

Critères : Décrit clairement le contexte et le problème ; Explique la solution mise en œuvre et son résultat ; Tire une leçon ou une conclusion ; Emploie correctement le prétérit et quelques connecteurs (because, so, then, finally) ; Discours suivi, compréhensible, avec un vocabulaire professionnel adapté
Réponse modèle : Last year, I was responsible for organising a training day for twenty new employees. Two days before the event, the trainer called me to say she was ill and couldn't come. At first I panicked, because the programme was already printed and everyone had booked the day. So I contacted two experienced colleagues, and they agreed to run the morning session. Then I asked the training company to send a replacement for the afternoon, and they found someone the same day. In the end, the feedback was very positive. What I learned is that you should always have a plan B, so now I keep a list of internal colleagues who can step in at short notice.

Exercice 5 — PL-C3-05 (C3, B2.2)

Préparez-vous 45 secondes, puis répondez à voix haute pendant 90 secondes. Donnez un avis argumenté et nuancé. Réponse corrigée par le formateur.

Question : Some companies are asking employees to return to the office full-time, while others are keeping remote work. What is your opinion on remote work? Give reasons and examples to support your view. (préparation 45 s, réponse 90 s)

Langue utile : In my view… / I'd argue that… · On the one hand… On the other hand… · That said, … · This is particularly true when… · A good example of this is… · What matters is not… but… · All things considered, …

Corrigé

Critères : Exprime un avis clair dès le début ; Développe au moins deux arguments illustrés par des exemples ; Nuance son propos (concession, limites, conditions) ; Utilise des connecteurs variés (however, on the other hand, that said, as a result) ; Vocabulaire précis et structures variées, peu d'hésitations ; Conclut en reformulant sa position
Réponse modèle : In my view, a hybrid model is clearly the most effective option, although I don't think there's a single answer for every company. On the one hand, remote work has real advantages. People save time on commuting, and for tasks that need concentration, such as writing a report or analysing data, working from home is often more productive. In my previous job, our team actually completed projects faster after we introduced two remote days a week. On the other hand, full-time remote work has hidden costs. New employees learn a lot simply by listening to experienced colleagues, and that's much harder over video calls. Creativity also suffers: many good ideas come from informal conversations that never happen online. That said, forcing everyone back to the office five days a week sends a message of mistrust and may push talented people to leave. So I'd argue that the best approach is to agree on shared office days for collaboration and leave the rest flexible. What matters is not where people work, but whether the organisation of work is clear and fair.

sections.title: C4 — Rédiger en anglais avec un vocabulaire et des tournures grammaticales appropriées
sections.contentHtml:
Exercice 1 — PL-GV-01 (C4, A2.1)

Choisissez le mot ou groupe de mots qui complète correctement le courriel.

Hi Mark,

I [1] _____ in the office today because I am ill. I [2] _____ back tomorrow. Can you [3] _____ the team meeting to Thursday, please?

Thanks,
Julie

[1] not am / am not / don't / isn't

[2] will be / am be / was / be

[3] moving / moves / to move / move

Corrigé

[1] am not. Négation de « be » avec « I » : « I am not ». « Don't » s'emploie avec les autres verbes, pas avec « be ».
[2] will be. « Tomorrow » appelle le futur : « I will be back ». « Was » renvoie au passé.
[3] move. Après « can », verbe à la base verbale sans « to » : « Can you move… ».

Exercice 2 — PL-GV-03 (C4, A2.2)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement la réponse à un client.

Dear Mr Lee,

Thank you for your email. I'm sorry, but Ms Grant [1] _____ a meeting at the moment. She [2] _____ to Paris last week for a conference, and she [3] _____ in the office again next Monday. Could you call [4] _____ on Tuesday morning?

Best regards,
Tina

[1] was in / goes to / has in / is in

[2] goes / has gone / went / going

[3] was / will be / is being / has been

[4] her / she / hers / herself

Corrigé

[1] is in. « At the moment » : situation actuelle, donc présent « is in a meeting ».
[2] went. « Last week » est un moment passé terminé : prétérit « went ». Le present perfect ne s'emploie pas avec « last week ».
[3] will be. « Next Monday » : futur, « she will be in the office ».
[4] her. Après un verbe, pronom complément : « call her ». « She » est un pronom sujet.

Exercice 3 — PL-GV-05 (C4, B1.1)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement le courriel.

Hi Sophie,

I'm writing to let you know that the delivery [1] _____ yet. The supplier says it [2] _____ by Friday. If it doesn't, we'll need to find another solution, [3] _____ the client is expecting the goods next week. I'll keep you [4] _____.

Best,
Omar

[1] hasn't arrived / didn't arrive / doesn't arrive / isn't arrived

[2] should arriving / must to arrive / would arrived / should arrive

[3] although / so / because / unless

[4] update / updated / updating / to update

Corrigé

[1] hasn't arrived. « Yet » s'emploie avec le present perfect : « hasn't arrived yet ». Le prétérit « didn't arrive » ne se combine pas naturellement avec « yet » en anglais britannique.
[2] should arrive. Modal + base verbale : « should arrive » (probabilité). « Must to » est fautif : pas de « to » après un modal.
[3] because. On donne la raison de l'urgence : « because the client is expecting the goods ». « So » introduirait une conséquence.
[4] updated. Expression figée « I'll keep you updated » (je vous tiens informé), avec le participe passé.

Exercice 4 — PL-GV-07 (C4, B1.2)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement le courriel commercial.

Dear Ms Park,

Further to our phone call, please find [1] _____ the updated price list. As you will see, our prices have [2] _____ by 3% since January. However, if you place your order [3] _____ the end of the month, we will offer you free delivery.

I look forward to [4] _____ from you.

Kind regards,
Leo Marsh

[1] attach / attached / attaching / to attach

[2] risen / raised / rose / arisen

[3] until / since / during / before

[4] hear / heard / hearing / be hearing

Corrigé

[1] attached. Formule figée « please find attached… » (veuillez trouver ci-joint), avec le participe passé.
[2] risen. « Rise » est intransitif (les prix augmentent d'eux-mêmes) ; present perfect : « have risen ». « Raised » exige un complément (« we have raised our prices »).
[3] before. Date limite : « before the end of the month ». « Until » indique une durée qui se prolonge, pas une échéance.
[4] hearing. Dans « look forward to », « to » est une préposition : il faut la forme en -ing.

Exercice 5 — PL-GV-09 (C4, B2.1)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement l'extrait de rapport d'incident.

Had we [1] _____ the problem earlier, we could have avoided the delay. Going forward, all orders [2] _____ by two people before they are sent. I would also suggest [3] _____ a written confirmation from each supplier within 24 hours. [4] _____ these measures in place, we expect errors to fall significantly.

[1] identify / identified / been identifying / to identify

[2] will be checked / will check / are checking / have checked

[3] to request / request / requested / requesting

[4] Despite / Unless / With / Although

Corrigé

[1] identified. Conditionnel passé avec inversion : « Had we identified » = « If we had identified ».
[2] will be checked. Les commandes subissent l'action : passif futur « will be checked ». « Will check » ferait des commandes le sujet actif.
[3] requesting. « Suggest » est suivi de -ing (ou de « that + sujet »), jamais de « to + verbe ».
[4] With. « With these measures in place » = une fois ces mesures en place. « Despite » exprimerait une opposition illogique ici.

Exercice 6 — PL-GV-11 (C4, B2.2)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement ce courriel de remerciement.

[1] _____ the delays caused by the strike, the shipment arrived on schedule. Not only [2] _____ the goods in perfect condition, but the supplier had also included a discount voucher. It is the first time this year that we [3] _____ such good service. We would be grateful [4] _____ you could pass on our thanks to the logistics team.

[1] Although / Despite / However / Even

[2] were / was / did / are

[3] received / receive / had received / have received

[4] that / whether / if / when

Corrigé

[1] Despite. « Despite » + groupe nominal (« the delays »). « Although » exige une proposition avec verbe conjugué.
[2] were. « Not only » en tête de phrase entraîne l'inversion : « Not only were the goods… » ; sujet pluriel et récit au passé.
[3] have received. « It is the first time that » + present perfect. Le prétérit « received » est l'erreur classique des francophones.
[4] if. Formule de politesse « We would be grateful if you could… ».

Exercice 7 — PL-GV-13 (C4, C1.1)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement cette note de la direction.

Were the merger [1] _____ ahead, around 300 roles could be affected. [2] _____ the board has yet to reach a decision, staff are understandably anxious. It is essential that communication be handled [3] _____, lest rumours [4] _____ the process. Only once the review is complete [5] _____ a formal announcement.

[1] going / to go / go / gone

[2] As / Despite / However / Unless

[3] sensitive / sensitivity / sensible / sensitively

[4] undermines / undermined / undermine / undermining

[5] the company will make / will the company make / will make the company / the company makes

Corrigé

[1] to go. Hypothèse formelle « Were + sujet + to + verbe » = « If the merger were to go ahead ».
[2] As. Lien de cause : c'est parce que le conseil n'a pas encore tranché que le personnel s'inquiète. « Despite » serait suivi d'un nom et illogique.
[3] sensitively. Adverbe qui modifie « handled » : « sensitively » (avec tact). « Sensible » est un faux ami (raisonnable).
[4] undermine. « Lest » est suivi du subjonctif, donc de la base verbale sans -s : « lest rumours undermine ».
[5] will the company make. « Only once… » en tête de phrase entraîne l'inversion auxiliaire-sujet dans la principale : « will the company make ».

Exercice 8 — PL-GV-15 (C4, C1.2)

Choisissez la forme qui complète correctement cet éditorial interne.

Little [1] _____ the team realise how far-reaching the consequences of the decision would be. Had the risks been properly assessed at the time, the company [2] _____ now be facing such heavy losses. It is high time the board [3] _____ responsibility for what happened. What is needed now is not further reassurance [4] _____ a credible recovery plan.

[1] did / had / were / have

[2] will not / had not / should not have / would not

[3] take / takes / took / has taken

[4] than / but / rather / and

Corrigé

[1] did. « Little » négatif en tête de phrase entraîne l'inversion avec l'auxiliaire « did » : « Little did the team realise ».
[2] would not. Conditionnel mixte : condition passée (« had been assessed ») et conséquence présente (« now ») : « would not now be facing ».
[3] took. « It is high time + sujet + prétérit » : le prétérit exprime ici un irréel du présent.
[4] but. Structure « not X but Y » (non pas X mais Y). « Rather » s'emploierait dans « rather than ».

Exercice 9 — PL-C4-01 (C4, B1.1)

Rédigez le courriel demandé en 20 minutes, en au moins 150 mots. Production corrigée par le formateur.

Sujet : Your team is moving to a new office next month. Write an email to your colleagues to explain the move. Include: the date and the new address, what they need to do before the move, and what will be different in the new office. (Rappel : écrivez un courriel structuré à vos collègues, au moins 150 mots, en traitant les trois points demandés.)

email — 150 mots minimum, 20 minutes

  • J'ai indiqué la date et l'adresse
  • J'ai expliqué ce que les collègues doivent faire avant le déménagement
  • J'ai décrit au moins deux changements
  • J'ai utilisé des paragraphes et des connecteurs
  • J'ai relu les temps verbaux et l'orthographe
  • Mon texte fait au moins 150 mots

Corrigé

Critères : Respect du sujet : les trois points (date et adresse, actions à faire, changements) sont traités ; Organisation : objet, salutation, paragraphes, formule de clôture ; Cohérence : connecteurs (first, also, however, finally, so) ; Grammaire : temps adaptés (futur, impératif poli, present perfect), accords ; Vocabulaire professionnel adapté et suffisamment varié ; Longueur : au moins 150 mots
Production modèle :
Subject: Our move to the new office on 14 November

Hi everyone,

As you know, our team is moving to a new office next month. I'd like to give you some practical information so that the move goes smoothly.

The move will take place on Friday 14 November. From Monday 17 November, we will work at 25 Harbour Street, on the fourth floor. The building is a ten-minute walk from Central Station, and there is a car park behind it.

Before the move, please do three things. First, clear your desk and put your personal items in the boxes that Facilities will deliver on 10 November. Second, label every box with your name and team. Finally, save all your files on the shared drive, because our computers will be reset.

There will also be some changes in the new office. We will not have fixed desks any more, so you will need to book a desk using the new app. However, there will be four meeting rooms instead of one, and a much bigger kitchen.

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Best regards,
Claire
